function _sesh_attach_or_switch() {
    local session="$1"
    if [[ -n "$TMUX" ]]; then
        tmux switch-client -t "$session"
    else
        tmux attach-session -t "$session"
    fi
}

# Create (or no-op if exists) a detached tmux session at the given path.
# Returns 0 if the session already existed, 1 if newly created. (Caller uses
# this to decide whether to apply layout setup or just attach.)
function _sesh_ensure_session() {
    local session="$1" target="$2"
    if tmux has-session -t "=$session" 2>/dev/null; then
        return 0   # already exists
    fi
    tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$target"
    return 1       # newly created
}

Tradeoff: one more bespoke function to maintain; no queueing / log persistence beyond what tmux's scrollback gives you.
2. **Just use `pueue add`** (you already have `36_pueue.zsh`) and skip tmux — `pueue follow` to peek, `pueue log` later. Better if the goal is really "I want logs I can read later." Worse if you genuinely want a live interactive pty to grab back (auth prompts, REPLs, dev servers you'll poke at).
3. **`zellij run --name foo --close-on-exit cmd`** — but that's zellij, not tmux, and you're set up with tmux as the primary multiplexer.

### 2. Autoname Pattern: Path → Session Name

From `sesh-here` (lines 189) and `sesh-root` / `sesh-code` / `sesh-vibe`:

```zsh

# sesh-vibe pattern (lines 586–588):

```

**Pattern for `tmrun`**: `_sesh_sanitize "$(basename "$PWD")"` for a simple auto-derived name, or parameterize like scode/svibe for a prefix-based pattern.

### 3. Exact `tmux new-session -d` Invocations

**sesh-code** (line 356): Creates editor window with named pane
```zsh
tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$repo_root" -n editor "$nvim_cmd"
```

**sesh-vibe** (lines 608–609): Creates agents window with first pane command
```zsh
tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$repo_root" -n agents \
    "$(_vibe_agent_cmd "${agents[1]}")"
```

**Key patterns**:
- `-d` (detached), `-s <session_name>`, `-c <working_dir>` (all mandatory for your use case)
- `-n <window_name>` (optional; if omitted, default window is `0`)
- Command string at the end is **unquoted in the tmux invocation** (variable expansion happens in the caller)
- The wrapped command (`$nvim_cmd`, `$agent_cmd`, etc.) is already a fully-formed shell string (see `_sesh_on_exit_wrap` return); passed bare to tmux

**For `tmrun` with `$@` passthrough**: you'd want something like:
```zsh
tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$PWD" "$@"
```
(If you want to wrap the command similarly to scode/svibe, build it first with `_sesh_on_exit_wrap` then pass the result.)

67	}

69	# Create (or no-op if exists) a detached tmux session at the given path.
70	# Returns 0 if the session already existed, 1 if newly created. (Caller uses
71	# this to decide whether to apply layout setup or just attach.)
72	function _sesh_ensure_session() {
73	    local session="$1" target="$2"
74	    if tmux has-session -t "=$session" 2>/dev/null; then
75	        return 0   # already exists
76	    fi
77	    tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$target"
78	    return 1       # newly created
79	}
80	
81	# Wrap a known specstory provider in `specstory run X` so the agent picks up
82	# auto-save markdown logging. Bare CLI names that aren't specstory providers
83	# (currently: opencode — see backlog/specstory-opencode-support.md) pass
84	# through unchanged.
85	#
86	# Update the case list when specstory adds providers (track upstream:
87	# specstoryai/getspecstory#146 for opencode, similar issues for others).
88	#
89	# Args: $1=agent, $2=specstory_mode (auto|never; default auto)
90	#   auto  — wrap if known provider, raw otherwise (the historical default)
91	#   never — pass through raw regardless (CLI flag --no-specstory sets this)
92	function _sesh_wrap_agent() {
93	    local agent="$1" specstory_mode="${2:-auto}"
94	    if [[ "$specstory_mode" == "never" ]]; then
95	        # Even an empty agent goes raw → caller's responsibility to pick a
96	        # sensible default (we choose `claude` upstream when --no-specstory
97	        # is set, since `specstory run` with no arg defaults to claude too).
98	        print -r -- "${agent:-claude}"
99	        return
100	    fi
101	    case "$agent" in
102	        ""|"specstory")
103	            # No agent specified → bare `specstory run` (default = claude).
104	            print -r -- "specstory run"
105	            ;;
106	        claude|codex|cursor|droid|gemini)
107	            print -r -- "specstory run $agent"
108	            ;;
109	        *)
110	            # Pass-through for non-specstory providers (opencode today, more
111	            # later as specstory adds support).
112	            print -r -- "$agent"
113	            ;;
114	    esac
115	}
116	
117	# Build a wrapper command that controls what happens when the inner command
118	# exits (Ctrl+C, agent quit, crash). `--on-exit shell|kill|restart`:
119	#   shell   — print a hint, then drop into $SHELL so user can restart agent,
120	#             switch to lazygit, kill the pane manually, etc. (default)
121	#   kill    — let the pane close on exit (tmux default `remain-on-exit off`)
122	#   restart — wrap in `while true; do CMD; sleep 1; done` so the agent
123	#             auto-respawns. Use Ctrl+C twice quickly to break the loop and
124	#             land in shell.
125	#
126	# Args: $1=inner_cmd, $2=mode, $3=label_for_hint
127	# Stdout: the wrapped shell command (single string suitable for `tmux
128	# new-window … "<cmd>"`). Quoting is structured so user $SHELL is the one
129	# evaluating the inner command — we don't double-eval.
130	function _sesh_on_exit_wrap() {
131	    local inner="$1" mode="$2" label="${3:-agent}"
132	    # Ctrl+C sends SIGINT to the entire foreground process group, so the
133	    # wrapper shell itself dies before it can print the hint or exec the
134	    # login shell — the pane just vanishes. `trap '' INT` makes the wrapper
135	    # ignore SIGINT; the inner command still receives it and exits normally,
136	    # then control returns to the wrapper which prints the hint as intended.
137	    # (Tools that install their own SIGINT handler — btop, htop, less — were
138	    # the visible failure case; agent CLIs happened to handle Ctrl+C as
139	    # clean exit so this was masked for them.)
140	    local guard="trap '' INT;"
141	    case "$mode" in
142	        kill)
143	            print -r -- "$inner"
144	            ;;
145	        restart)
146	            # `|| true` so a crash exit doesn't abort the loop on `set -e` shells
147	            print -r -- "$guard while true; do $inner || true; echo '[$label exited — respawning in 1s; Ctrl+C twice to break]'; sleep 1; done; exec \$SHELL -l"
148	            ;;
149	        shell|*)
150	            # Default. Hint message uses tmux color codes — works in all
151	            # terminals tmux supports.
152	            print -r -- "$guard $inner; printf '\\n\\033[33m[$label exited — back in shell. Re-run with: \\033[1m%s\\033[0;33m]\\033[0m\\n' \"$inner\"; exec \$SHELL -l"
153	            ;;
154	    esac
155	}
156	
157	# Connect to a sesh session for the current directory (creates it if missing).
158	# Lightweight: drops you into a plain shell at $PWD with NO startup command.
159	# For an editor-first session use `scode` (repo-aware, full layout) or just
160	# launch nvim manually inside the new session.
161	#
162	# Smart argument handling:
163	#   shere                              # plain shell at $PWD, no command
164	#   shere specstory run codex          # bare args → treated as command
165	#   shere -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
166	#   shere -p ~/my-proj                 # explicit path, plain shell
167	#   shere -p ~/my-proj npm run dev     # explicit path + command
168	function sesh-here() {
169	    local cmd="" target=""
170	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
171	        case "$1" in
172	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
173	            -p|--path)    target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
174	            -*)           echo "sesh-here: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
175	            *)            break ;;  # remaining args are the command
176	        esac
177	    done
178	    [[ $# -gt 0 && -z "$cmd" ]] && cmd="$*"
179	    target="${target:-$PWD}"
180	    if [[ -n "$cmd" ]]; then
181	        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$target"
182	    else
183	        # Bypass sesh's default_session.startup_command (nvim) for a plain
184	        # shell. We create the session via tmux directly, then attach. This
185	        # also means the wildcard startup_command (project layout) is
186	        # bypassed — `shere` is intentionally lightweight; use `scode`,
187	        # `svibe`, or `sesh connect <path>` for layouts.
188	        local session
189	        session=$(_sesh_sanitize "$(basename "$target")")
190	        _sesh_ensure_session "$session" "$target"
191	        _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
192	    fi
193	}
194	
195	# Connect to the current git root when available, otherwise use $PWD.
196	# Same smart argument handling as sesh-here.
197	#   sroot                              # default startup_command
198	#   sroot specstory run codex          # bare args → command
199	#   sroot -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
200	function sesh-root() {
201	    local cmd="" root
202	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
203	        case "$1" in
204	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
205	            -*)           shift ;;
206	            *)            break ;;
207	        esac
208	    done
209	    [[ $# -gt 0 && -z "$cmd" ]] && cmd="$*"
210	    root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || root=$PWD
211	    if [[ -n "$cmd" ]]; then
212	        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$root"
213	    else
214	        sesh connect "$root"
215	    fi
216	}
217	
218	alias shere='sesh-here'
219	alias sroot='sesh-root'
220	alias scode='sesh-code'
221	alias svibe='sesh-vibe'
222	
223	# ── scode: repo-aware coding-agent layout ───────────────────────────────────
224	#
225	# Open the coding-agent layout (nvim 75% | specstory-wrapped agent 25%, btop
226	# window) in a session NAMED FOR THE CURRENT REPO, so different repos don't
227	# collide on the single `coding-agent` session name.
228	#
229	# Session naming:
230	#   In repo /Volumes/Data/Program/Personal/foo  → session `coding-agent/foo`
231	#   Same repo re-invocation                     → attach (no duplicate)
232	#   Different repo                              → new session `coding-agent/<other>`
233	#
234	# Outside a git repo the function refuses with a hint to use `shere` or `svibe`
235	# (the heavy layout doesn't make sense for ad-hoc directories).
236	#
237	# Agent wrapping: known specstory providers (claude/codex/cursor/droid/gemini)
238	# are auto-wrapped in `specstory run X` for markdown auto-save. Others
239	# (opencode today) pass through raw — see _sesh_wrap_agent + backlog entry
240	# `specstory-opencode-support` for the upstream tracking.
241	#
242	# Exit behavior: `--on-exit shell` (default) drops to a shell with a hint when
243	# the agent exits, so Ctrl+C doesn't kill the pane. Use `--on-exit kill` for
244	# the old behavior, or `--on-exit restart` for an auto-respawn loop.
245	#
246	# Usage:
247	#   scode                              # current repo, default agent (specstory → claude)
248	#   scode codex                        # specstory run codex
249	#   scode opencode                     # opencode raw (not yet a specstory provider)
250	#   scode --on-exit kill claude        # Ctrl+C kills the right pane
251	#   scode --on-exit restart codex      # codex auto-respawns on crash
252	#   scode -p ~/some/other/repo         # explicit repo path
253	#   scode --no-attach                  # create session in background, don't switch
254	function sesh-code() {
255	    local target="" agent="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto"
256	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
257	        case "$1" in
258	            -p|--path)      target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
259	            -a|--agent)     agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
260	            --on-exit)      on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
261	            --no-specstory) specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
262	            --specstory)    specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
263	            --no-attach)    no_attach=1; shift ;;
264	            --agents)
265	                echo "scode: --agents is svibe-only (scode is single-agent)." >&2
266	                echo "       For multi-agent layouts: svibe --agents '$2'" >&2
267	                return 1 ;;
268	            -h|--help)
269	                cat <<'EOF'
270	scode — open repo-scoped coding-agent layout
271	
272	Usage: scode [--path DIR] [--agent CLI] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory]
273	             [--no-attach] [AGENT]
274	
275	Layout: window `editor` (nvim 75% | agent 25%) + window `monitor` (btop).
276	Session name: `coding-agent/<repo-basename>` (one session per repo).
277	Requires:     git repo (errors otherwise — use `shere` or `svibe`).
278	
279	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
280	  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
281	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
282	
283	--on-exit MODE controls what happens when ANY pane command exits/Ctrl+C
284	(applies to the agent pane, the nvim pane, and the btop monitor window):
285	  shell    (default) — drop to shell with a hint, command re-runnable
286	  kill                — let the pane/window close (tmux default)
287	  restart             — auto-respawn the command in a loop
288	
289	Examples:
290	  scode                            # current repo, default agent (specstory → claude)
291	  scode codex                      # right pane: specstory run codex
292	  scode opencode                   # right pane: opencode (raw)
293	  scode --no-specstory claude      # right pane: claude (raw, no markdown auto-save)
294	  scode --on-exit kill claude      # right pane closes when claude exits
295	  scode -p ~/work/foo              # explicit repo path
296	EOF
297	                return 0 ;;
298	            -*)             echo "scode: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
299	            *)              [[ -z "$agent" ]] && agent="$1" || true; shift ;;
300	        esac
301	    done
302	
303	    case "$on_exit" in
304	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
305	        *) echo "scode: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
306	    esac
307	
308	    # Resolve repo root
309	    local repo_root
310	    if [[ -n "$target" ]]; then
311	        repo_root=$(cd "$target" 2>/dev/null && _sesh_git_root)
312	    else
313	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
314	    fi
315	    if [[ -z "$repo_root" ]]; then
316	        echo "scode: not inside a git repo." >&2
317	        echo "       Use \`shere\` for a plain shell, or \`svibe\` for a vibe layout in any dir." >&2
318	        return 1
319	    fi
320	
321	    # Validate agent CLI exists in PATH (fail-fast). Specstory itself isn't
322	    # checked here — if the user passed a known provider but specstory is
323	    # missing, the pane will exit with specstory's error message and
324	    # --on-exit=shell will leave a shell to read it.
325	    if [[ -n "$agent" ]] && ! command -v "$agent" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
326	        echo "scode: agent CLI '$agent' not found in PATH." >&2
327	        return 1
328	    fi
329	
330	    local repo_name session
331	    repo_name=$(basename "$repo_root")
332	    session=$(_sesh_sanitize "coding-agent/${repo_name}")
333	
334	    # If session already exists, just attach (idempotent — solves the
335	    # cross-repo collision problem the old single `coding-agent` session had).
336	    if tmux has-session -t "=$session" 2>/dev/null; then
337	        (( no_attach )) || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
338	        return 0
339	    fi
340	
341	    # Create session + build layout directly with tmux commands (see svibe
342	    # comment block for why not tmuxp).
343	    #
344	    # Window 1 "editor": nvim (left, will be 75%) | wrapped agent (right, 25%)
345	    # Window 2 "monitor": btop (or htop / top fallback)
346	    local agent_inner agent_cmd
347	    agent_inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$agent" "$specstory_mode")
348	    agent_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$agent_inner" "$on_exit" "${agent:-agent}")
349	
350	    # nvim and monitor get the same on-exit treatment as the agent so that
351	    # quitting them drops to a shell with a re-launch hint instead of the
352	    # pane/window vanishing.
353	    local nvim_cmd monitor_inner monitor_cmd
354	    nvim_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")
355	
356	    tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$repo_root" -n editor "$nvim_cmd"
357	    tmux split-window -h -t "${session}:editor" -c "$repo_root" "$agent_cmd"
358	    # main-vertical layout, then size the LEFT pane to 75% of window width
359	    tmux select-layout -t "${session}:editor" main-vertical >/dev/null
360	    tmux resize-pane -t "${session}:editor.1" -x 75% 2>/dev/null
361	
362	    # Monitor window
363	    if   command -v btop >/dev/null 2>&1; then monitor_inner=btop
364	    elif command -v htop >/dev/null 2>&1; then monitor_inner=htop
365	    else                                       monitor_inner=top
366	    fi
367	    monitor_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$monitor_inner" "$on_exit" "$monitor_inner")
368	    tmux new-window -t "$session" -n monitor -c "$repo_root" "$monitor_cmd"
369	
370	    # Focus editor window, left (nvim) pane
371	    tmux select-window -t "${session}:editor"
372	    tmux select-pane -t "${session}:editor.1"
373	
374	    (( no_attach )) || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
375	}
376	
377	# ── svibe: parametric multi-agent vibe layout ───────────────────────────────
378	#
379	# A "vibe coding" session: window 1 has N agent panes (default 4), window 2
380	# is lazygit, window 3 is nvim. Built directly with tmux split/new-window
381	# commands so it stays parametric (tmuxp YAML can't express dynamic pane counts).
382	#
383	# Session naming: `vibe/<dir-basename>` — collision-safe across directories.
384	# Refuses outside a git repo (use `shere` for plain shells in arbitrary dirs).
385	#
386	# Each agent pane is wrapped in `specstory run X` (for known providers, opt
387	# out with --no-specstory) and additionally wrapped in an exit handler
388	# controlled by `--on-exit MODE` — same semantics as `scode`. Default `shell`
389	# keeps the pane open with a hint after the agent exits, so Ctrl+C is
390	# recoverable.
391	#
392	# Two modes for choosing which agents run:
393	#   1. Homogeneous (positional): `svibe 4 codex` → 4 panes all running codex
394	#   2. Heterogeneous (--agents):  `svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode`
395	#                                 → 4 panes running those specific agents
396	#                                 (list LENGTH determines pane count;
397	#                                 positional N_AGENTS is rejected to avoid
398	#                                 ambiguity)
399	#
400	# Usage:
401	#   svibe                                          # 4× claude (specstory)
402	#   svibe 2                                        # 2× claude
403	#   svibe 4 codex                                  # 4× specstory run codex
404	#   svibe 3 opencode                               # 3× opencode (raw)
405	#   svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode     # 4 panes, mixed
406	#   svibe --agents claude,opencode --on-exit kill  # 2 panes, mixed, hard exit
407	#   svibe --no-specstory 4 claude                  # 4× claude (raw, no md auto-save)
408	#   svibe --on-exit restart 4 codex                # auto-respawn loop
409	#   svibe -p ~/repo 4 claude                       # explicit path
410	#   svibe --no-attach 4 claude                     # create in background
411	function sesh-vibe() {
412	    local target="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto"
413	    local n_agents=4 n_agents_set=0
414	    local agent_cli="claude"
415	    local agents_csv=""
416	    local min_width="${SVIBE_MIN_WIDTH:-80}"
417	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
418	        case "$1" in
419	            -p|--path)      target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
420	            --on-exit)      on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
421	            --agents)       agents_csv="$2"; shift 2 ;;
422	            --min-width)    min_width="$2"; shift 2 ;;
423	            --no-specstory) specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
424	            --specstory)    specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
425	            --no-attach)    no_attach=1; shift ;;
426	            -h|--help)
427	                cat <<'EOF'
428	svibe — parametric multi-agent vibe layout
429	
430	Usage:
431	  svibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
432	        [--min-width COLS] [N_AGENTS] [AGENT_CLI]
433	  svibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
434	        [--min-width COLS] --agents A1,A2,A3[,...]
435	
436	Default: svibe           (N auto-picked from term_width ÷ min-width, clamp [1,12])
437	  window 1 "agents" — N agent panes (columns if all fit at ≥min-width, else tiled)
438	  window 2 "git"    — lazygit
439	  window 3 "edit"   — nvim
440	
441	Two modes for choosing agents:
442	  Homogeneous:    `svibe 4 codex` → 4 panes all codex
443	  Heterogeneous:  `svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode`
444	                  → 4 panes (one each, in order); list length = pane count
445	
446	Session name: `vibe/<repo-basename>` (collision-safe per directory).
447	Requires:     git repo (use `shere` for plain shells elsewhere).
448	
449	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
450	  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
451	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
452	
453	--on-exit MODE controls per-pane behavior on Ctrl+C / clean exit
454	(applies to all agent panes, the lazygit window, and the nvim window):
455	  shell    (default) — drop to shell with a hint, command re-runnable
456	  kill                — let the pane/window close (tmux default)
457	  restart             — auto-respawn the command in a loop
458	
459	--min-width COLS sets the minimum readable per-pane width (default: value of
460	$SVIBE_MIN_WIDTH, else 80). It drives two decisions:
461	  • auto-pick N when you don't pass a count (N = term_width / min-width)
462	  • columns vs tiled in the agents window: columns when all N panes fit at
463	    ≥COLS wide side-by-side, otherwise tiled grid
464	Example on a 240-col terminal:
465	  min-width 80   → auto N=3, three even-horizontal columns
466	  min-width 120  → auto N=2, two even-horizontal columns
467	
468	Examples:
469	  svibe                                            # auto N × claude, width-aware layout
470	  svibe 2                                          # 2× claude
471	  svibe 4 codex                                    # 4× codex
472	  svibe 6 opencode                                 # 6× opencode (heavy)
473	  svibe --min-width 120                            # wider panes → fewer auto columns
474	  svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode       # 4 panes, mixed
475	  svibe --agents claude,opencode --on-exit kill    # 2 panes, mixed
476	  svibe --no-specstory 4 claude                    # raw claude, no auto-save
477	EOF
478	                return 0 ;;
479	            -*)             echo "svibe: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
480	            *)              break ;;
481	        esac
482	    done
483	
484	    if ! [[ "$min_width" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( min_width < 1 )); then
485	        echo "svibe: --min-width must be a positive integer (got: $min_width)" >&2
486	        return 1
487	    fi
488	
489	    # Current terminal width, used for auto-picking N (when the user didn't
490	    # pass a count) and for the columns-vs-tiled cutover. $COLUMNS is
491	    # auto-maintained by zsh on SIGWINCH; tput is a fallback for corner cases
492	    # (e.g. non-interactive invocation); 200 is a generous last resort.
493	    local term_width="${COLUMNS:-$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || echo 200)}"
494	
495	    # Build the agents array. Two paths:
496	    #   --agents claude,codex,…  → split csv, list length = pane count
497	    #   positional [N] [CLI]     → repeat CLI N times (N auto-picked if omitted)
498	    # Mixing both is rejected to keep semantics unambiguous.
499	    local -a agents
500	    if [[ -n "$agents_csv" ]]; then
501	        if [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
502	            echo "svibe: cannot combine --agents with positional N_AGENTS/AGENT_CLI." >&2
503	            echo "       Pick one. (e.g. drop the trailing args)" >&2
504	            return 1
505	        fi
506	        # Split CSV. Trim whitespace per element so 'claude, codex' works.
507	        local IFS=','
508	        agents=( ${=agents_csv} )
509	        # Trim leading/trailing whitespace on each element
510	        local j
511	        for (( j = 1; j <= ${#agents}; j++ )); do
512	            agents[$j]="${agents[$j]## }"
513	            agents[$j]="${agents[$j]%% }"
514	        done
515	        if (( ${#agents} == 0 )); then
516	            echo "svibe: --agents list is empty." >&2
517	            return 1
518	        fi
519	    else
520	        # Positional: [n_agents] [agent_cli]
521	        if [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
522	            if [[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
523	                n_agents="$1"; n_agents_set=1; shift
524	            fi
525	        fi
526	        [[ $# -gt 0 ]] && agent_cli="$1"
527	
528	        # Auto-pick N from terminal width when the user didn't pass one.
529	        # N = clamp(term_width / min_width, 1, 12). On a 240-col terminal
530	        # with min-width 80 that's N=3; at min-width 120, N=2.
531	        if (( ! n_agents_set )); then
532	            n_agents=$(( term_width / min_width ))
533	            (( n_agents < 1 )) && n_agents=1
534	            (( n_agents > 12 )) && n_agents=12
535	        fi
536	
537	        # Build a homogeneous array of length n_agents
538	        local k
539	        for (( k = 1; k <= n_agents; k++ )); do
540	            agents+=( "$agent_cli" )
541	        done
542	    fi
543	
544	    case "$on_exit" in
545	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
546	        *) echo "svibe: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
547	    esac
548	
549	    if (( ${#agents} < 1 || ${#agents} > 12 )); then
550	        echo "svibe: agent count = ${#agents} out of range [1, 12]" >&2
551	        return 1
552	    fi
553	
554	    # Resolve repo root
555	    local repo_root
556	    if [[ -n "$target" ]]; then
557	        repo_root=$(cd "$target" 2>/dev/null && _sesh_git_root)
558	    else
559	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
560	    fi
561	    if [[ -z "$repo_root" ]]; then
562	        echo "svibe: not inside a git repo." >&2
563	        echo "       Use \`shere\` for a plain shell in arbitrary directories." >&2
564	        return 1
565	    fi
566	
567	    # Validate ALL agent CLIs exist in PATH (fail-fast — we don't want to
568	    # build a 4-pane layout where one pane is dead). De-dup the list to keep
569	    # the error message readable.
570	    local -a missing
571	    local -A seen
572	    local a
573	    for a in "${agents[@]}"; do
574	        [[ -n "${seen[$a]:-}" ]] && continue
575	        seen[$a]=1
576	        if ! command -v "$a" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
577	            missing+=( "$a" )
578	        fi
579	    done
580	    if (( ${#missing} > 0 )); then
581	        echo "svibe: agent CLI(s) not found in PATH: ${missing[*]}" >&2
582	        echo "       Available: $(for c in claude codex opencode cursor droid gemini; do command -v $c >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo -n "$c "; done)" >&2
583	        return 1
584	    fi
585	
586	    local repo_name session
587	    repo_name=$(basename "$repo_root")
588	    session=$(_sesh_sanitize "vibe/${repo_name}")
589	
590	    # Idempotent: existing session = just attach
591	    if tmux has-session -t "=$session" 2>/dev/null; then
592	        (( no_attach )) || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
593	        return 0
594	    fi
595	
596	    # Build wrapped command for each agent (the wrapping is pane-specific so
597	    # we can mix providers in one window).
598	    #
599	    # Helper: turn agent name → fully-wrapped tmux command string.
600	    _vibe_agent_cmd() {
601	        local inner
602	        inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$1" "$specstory_mode")
603	        _sesh_on_exit_wrap "$inner" "$on_exit" "$1"
604	    }
605	
606	    # ── Build the session ───────────────────────────────────────────────
607	    # Window 1: agents (start with first pane running agents[1])
608	    tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$repo_root" -n agents \
609	        "$(_vibe_agent_cmd "${agents[1]}")"
610	
611	    # Pick window layout based on agent count vs what fits as readable
612	    # side-by-side columns at --min-width:
613	    #   N ≤ term_width / min_width → even-horizontal (columns)
614	    #   otherwise                  → tiled (grid — columns would be too narrow)
615	    local max_columns=$(( term_width / min_width ))
616	    (( max_columns < 1 )) && max_columns=1
617	    local svibe_layout
618	    if (( ${#agents} <= max_columns )); then
619	        svibe_layout="even-horizontal"
620	    else
621	        svibe_layout="tiled"
622	    fi
623	
624	    # Add remaining panes
625	    local i
626	    for (( i = 2; i <= ${#agents}; i++ )); do
627	        tmux split-window -t "${session}:agents" -c "$repo_root" \
628	            "$(_vibe_agent_cmd "${agents[$i]}")"
629	        # Re-balance after each split so layout stays uniform
630	        tmux select-layout -t "${session}:agents" "$svibe_layout" >/dev/null
631	    done
632	
633	    unset -f _vibe_agent_cmd
634	
635	    # Window 2: git (lazygit if present)
636	    # lazygit and nvim get the same on-exit handling as agents — quitting
637	    # them drops to shell with a re-launch hint rather than killing the window.
638	    local git_cmd edit_cmd
639	    if command -v lazygit >/dev/null 2>&1; then
640	        git_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "lazygit" "$on_exit" "lazygit")
641	        tmux new-window -t "$session" -n git -c "$repo_root" "$git_cmd"
642	    else
643	        # `git status; exec $SHELL` already lands in shell — no wrap needed.
644	        tmux new-window -t "$session" -n git -c "$repo_root" "git status; exec \$SHELL"
645	    fi
646	
647	    # Window 3: edit (nvim)
648	    edit_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")
649	    tmux new-window -t "$session" -n edit -c "$repo_root" "$edit_cmd"
650	
651	    # Focus agents window, first pane
652	    tmux select-window -t "${session}:agents"
653	    tmux select-pane -t "${session}:agents.1"
654	
655	    (( no_attach )) || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
656	}
657	
658	# Register as zsh widget
659	zle -N sesh-sessions
660	
661	# Key bindings (Alt+S for session switcher, avoids conflict with Ctrl+A tmux prefix)
662	bindkey -M emacs '\es' sesh-sessions
663	bindkey -M viins '\es' sesh-sessions
664	bindkey -M vicmd '\es' sesh-sessions
665
```

522	### Proxy helpers
523	
524	> Portable loopback-proxy helpers. Honors `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` (+ optional `$LOCAL_PROXY_SOCKS_URL` for split Clash `socks-port:` configs); otherwise prefers an active Clash config (`mixed-port:` or `port:`/`socks-port:` from `~/.config/clash/config.yaml` or `~/Library/Application Support/clash/config.yaml`) before falling back to probing ports 7890/7891/1087/8118/8080 with `nc -z -w1`. Detection is cached per shell; `proxy-off` and `proxy-refresh` clear that cache before the next lookup. Set `$LOCAL_PROXY_AUTO_ACTIVATE=1` to auto-export env vars on shell startup. Full guide: [docs/tools/web-reader.md](../tools/web-reader.md). See also: [docs/tools/containers.md](../tools/containers.md) for how `$LOCAL_PROXY_URL` feeds the chezmoi-managed `~/.docker/config.json` `proxies.default` block.
525

527	|---------|------|-------------|-------------|
528	| `withproxy` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh` | Run a single command with proxy env vars exported to the child only (e.g. `withproxy curl ...`) |
529	| `try_direct_then_proxy` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh` | Run a command direct; on failure, retry via `withproxy`. Used as the default for reader functions. |
530	| `proxy-on` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh` | Export `http_proxy`/`https_proxy`/`HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`/`ALL_PROXY` in the current shell |
531	| `proxy-off` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh` | Unset all proxy env vars in the current shell |
532	| `proxy-status` | function | `dot_config/zsh/tools/50_networking.zsh` | Report state: **active** (exported), **available** (detected), or **unavailable** |

1	# Dotfiles Repository — Agent Contract
2	
3	Cross-platform dotfiles managed by **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system deps). This file is the agent-facing contract: maintenance rules, hard invariants, and pointers to docs. User-facing intro is in [README.md](README.md).
4	
5	> **Headroom rule**: keep this file under ~30k chars. Push handbook content into `docs/`; keep only edit rules and cross-file invariants here.
6	
7	## Cross-file maintenance rules
8	
9	When you change one of these surfaces, update the listed mirror file in the same commit. These are the rules most often forgotten.
10	
11	### README.md
12	
13	When adding/modifying configurations, update [README.md](README.md):
14	
15	- **New config files** → "What You Get > Config Files" section
16	- **New ansible roles/tools** → "What You Get > Tools" section
17	- **New platforms** → "Supported Platforms" table
18	- **Changed setup steps** → "Quick Setup" section
19	
20	Keep README.md concise and user-focused. Technical details belong here or in `docs/`.
21	
22	### `docs/` + MkDocs site → `mkdocs.yml` nav
23	
24	`docs/` is published to **<https://daviddwlee84.github.io/dotfiles/>** via a MkDocs Material site (auto-deployed by [`.github/workflows/docs.yml`](.github/workflows/docs.yml) on push-to-main when `docs/**`, `mkdocs.yml`, `pyproject.toml`, or `uv.lock` changes). Source of truth remains the `.md` files in the repo; the site is a renderer.
25	
26	Any time you **add a new `docs/**/*.md` file**:
27	
28	1. Add a nav entry in [`mkdocs.yml`](mkdocs.yml) under the matching top-level section (Tools / Zsh / Neovim / This Repo / Infrastructure / Tutorials / Input methods / Misc). Alphabetical within a section unless there's a narrative order.
29	2. Cross-link from related pages if applicable (e.g., a new `docs/tools/foo.md` probably wants a mention in `docs/tools/tmux/README.md` or `docs/tools/sesh.md` if relevant).
30	3. Run `uv run mkdocs build --strict` locally to catch broken links / stale anchors. If you're adding *external*-relative links (to `dot_config/…`, `pitfalls/…`, `backlog/…`), the `validation.links.not_found: info` config tolerates them — that's intentional, don't tighten it without cleaning up the ~20 known anchor-drift cases tracked in [`backlog/mkdocs-anchor-drift.md`](backlog/mkdocs-anchor-drift.md) first.
31	
32	The `.claude/skills/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/add-docs-page.sh` helper can create a new page + insert the nav entry in one shot, but hand-editing `mkdocs.yml` is also fine as long as strict build passes.
33	
34	**What does NOT belong in `docs/`** (stays at repo root, NOT in MkDocs nav):
35	
36	| Surface | Why |
37	|---|---|
38	| `README.md` | Canonical GitHub landing page; `docs/index.md` links to it (no duplication, no snippet copy) |
39	| `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `GEMINI.md` | Agent-operational contract; `docs/for-maintainers.md` references it |
40	| `TODO.md`, `backlog/`, `pitfalls/` | Dynamic maintainer surfaces; `docs/for-maintainers.md` references them via absolute GitHub URLs (reference, not copy) |
41	| `NOTES.md` | User's personal WIP notes |
42	
43	All four categories are **referenced** from [`docs/for-maintainers.md`](docs/for-maintainers.md) via absolute GitHub URLs — do not add them to `mkdocs.yml` nav or include them via `pymdownx.snippets`. The "reference yes, copy no" rule avoids drift between the site and the live repo root.
44	
45	### Custom aliases & shell functions → `docs/zsh/aliases.md`
46	
47	When adding/modifying/removing a custom alias or shell function in any `dot_config/zsh/` file, update [`docs/zsh/aliases.md`](docs/zsh/aliases.md): one row per entry with command name, type (`alias` or `function`), source file (relative to repo root), and a one-line description.
48	
49	### `gui_apps_linux` ansible role → `docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md`
50	
51	When adding/modifying/removing a Linux GUI app in [`dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml`](dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/tasks/main.yml), update the **Inventory** table in [`docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md`](docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md). The playbook is the single source of truth for the per-app mechanism / auto-update story, and is the first thing a maintainer (or agent) should read before adding a new app — it contains the `.deb` / Snap / Flatpak / AppImage decision tree and the concrete copy-paste patterns. Read it first; update it in the same commit.
52	
53	### Dockerfile + dotfiles_init wrapper
54	
55	When adding new chezmoi prompts in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`, three files must be updated in the same commit:
56	
57	1. `Dockerfile` — add `ARG CHEZMOI_*` build argument, add `--promptBool` / `--promptString` flag to `chezmoi init`.
58	2. `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` — add a matching entry to the `PROMPTS` tuple (key, kind, group, label, desc, default).
59	3. (If the prompt should be part of any named bundle) `BUNDLES` dict in the same file.
60	
61	Verify parity with: `uv run --script scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py doctor`. The subcommand greps `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` + `Dockerfile` and compares against the embedded `PROMPTS`; non-zero exit means drift.
62	
63	### Agent artifact redaction
64	
65	SpecStory transcripts and coding-agent plan files commonly paste shell output, config snippets, or `.env` values that may contain secrets. Four directories are auto-scanned/redacted:
66	
67	| Prefix | Source |
68	|--------|--------|
69	| `.specstory/history/` | SpecStory chat transcripts |
70	| `.claude/plans/` | Claude Code plan files |
71	| `.cursor/plans/` | Cursor plan files |
72	| `.opencode/plans/` | OpenCode plan files |
73	
74	Tooling: `scripts/redact_secrets.py` (gitleaks + `PRIV***KEY` pattern), `just check-secrets` / `just redact-secrets` / `just add-and-redact`. Pre-commit hook `redact-agent-secrets` runs `--fix` before `gitleaks-system`; if it rewrites a file, stage and retry.
75	
76	When introducing a new coding-agent artifact directory that could contain secrets, add its prefix to `DEFAULT_PATHS` in `scripts/redact_secrets.py` **and** the `files:` regex of the `redact-agent-secrets` pre-commit hook.
77	
78	### Keyboard shortcuts (cross-tool conflict check)
79	
80	When adding/modifying keybindings in any tool config, cross-check against other tools — multiple tools share the terminal's key namespace, especially `Ctrl+` and `Alt+`.
81	
82	| Tool | Config file | Conflict risk |
83	|------|-------------|---------------|
84	| tmux (root-table) | `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf` | `C-h/j/k/l` (vim-tmux-navigator), `C-1..9` (window switch); `prefix + a` (live agent panes picker — `tv agent-panes`, see [docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md](docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md)) |
85	| Television (global) | `dot_config/television/config.toml` | `Ctrl+S/F/R/Y/T/X/O` (built-in actions) |
86	| Television (channels) | `dot_config/television/cable/*.toml` | Per-channel `[keybindings]` overrides global |
87	| Zellij | `dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` | Mitigated by `default_mode "locked"` |
88	| Ghostty | `dot_config/ghostty/config` | `macos-option-as-alt` affects `Alt+` availability |
89	| zsh ZLE widgets | `dot_config/zsh/tools/{11_tools_picker,12_television,22_sesh,05_aisuggest}.zsh` | `Alt+T/R/P/G/E/A/I/S` (pickers), `Alt+;` (aisuggest, configurable via `AISUGGEST_KEY`); rebound from `zvm_after_init` in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` to survive zsh-vi-mode's keybind wipe |
90	| Claude Code (TUI) | `dot_claude/modify_keybindings.json` (overlay) + `~/.claude/keybindings.json` (live); see [docs/tools/claude-code-keybindings.md](docs/tools/claude-code-keybindings.md) | `Ctrl+R` (history:search — collides with atuin / zsh-history-substring at the prompt outside Claude), `Ctrl+T` (toggleTodos — Television's `Ctrl+T` is shadowed when Claude has focus), `Ctrl+G` (chat:externalEditor), `Ctrl+S` (chat:stash), `Shift+Tab` (chat:cycleMode — only known mode-switch action, no jump-to-plan) |
91	
92	Known conflict zones: `Ctrl+H/J/K/L` (tmux vim-tmux-navigator; removed in TV global), `Ctrl+S/F/R` (TV built-in cycling/reload — avoid in channel actions), `Alt+*` (safe namespace for channel-specific actions; requires terminal to send Option as Meta). Free Alt slots in this repo: `Alt+/`, `Alt+\`, and most letters not listed above (B/D/F/H/J/K/L/M/N/O/Q/U/V/W/X/Y/Z) — but check `dot_config/zsh/tools/*.zsh` first before claiming a new one.
93	
94	**Resolution precedence**: tmux root-table bindings intercept keys before they reach the inner application. Inside tmux, any `bind-key -n C-*` shadows the same `ctrl-*` in TV. Prefer `Alt+` for custom actions.

133	
134	## Chezmoi templating conventions
135	
136	**Hard rule**: before adding a `{{ if eq .profile ... }}` branch, ask if the predicate is auto-detectable. If yes, use `.chezmoi.os` / `.chezmoi.arch` / `.chezmoi.hostname` instead. `.profile` exists only for user-role choices chezmoi cannot infer (server vs desktop).
137	
138	| Predicate | Use |
139	|---|---|
140	| Any macOS (Apple Silicon or Intel) | `eq .chezmoi.os "darwin"` |
141	| Any Linux | `eq .chezmoi.os "linux"` |
142	| Apple Silicon only | `eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64"` (inside darwin-scoped files) or `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64")` |
143	| Intel Mac only | `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "amd64")` |
144	| Desktop vs headless (user role) | `.profile` — `ubuntu_desktop` / `ubuntu_server`; macOS side covered by `eq .chezmoi.os "darwin"` |
145	
146	Profile values are intentionally limited to `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server`. **Do not** introduce new profile values for OS/arch facts (the historical `macos_intel` profile was removed for exactly this reason).
147	
148	Full decision table, before/after examples, and the `macos_intel` migration snippet: [docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md).
149	
150	## Hard repo invariants
151	
152	### Install vs upgrade is split on purpose
153	
154	`chezmoi apply` (+ ansible phase) is deliberately **install-only**: roles use `state: present` / `creates:` so re-applying never silently bumps every tool. The explicit upgrade path lives in [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](scripts/upgrade_tools.sh), exposed via `just upgrade-*` recipes.
155	
156	- **Do not** rewrite ansible roles to `state: latest`.
157	- **Do not** add `apt upgrade` / system package bumps to default scope.
158	- `scripts/**` is in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`, so `upgrade_tools.sh` is never deployed; it runs from the repo directly.
159	- Adding a new upgrade category: see [docs/this_repo/upgrades.md](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md) → "Adding a new category". For a tool already managed by an existing package manager (brew/uv/npm/cargo/dotnet/gem/mise) you do nothing — generic `upgrade` picks it up.
160	
161	Full per-category matrix, sample output, and troubleshooting: [docs/this_repo/upgrades.md](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md). The short version is also mirrored in `README.md`.
162	
163	### Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts
164	
165	All three `run_*` scripts share one sudo session via `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh`. The user is prompted **once** at the start of `chezmoi apply` and downstream scripts reuse the cached credential silently.
166	
167	**Hard rules** when touching run-scripts:
168	
169	- Do **not** re-implement `sudo -k` / `sudo -v` / TTY-read logic. Call the shared helper.
170	- Do **not** run `sudo -k` (invalidates the shared cache for the whole flow).
171	- Do **not** register a `trap … EXIT` that removes state (next run-script needs it).
172	- Do **not** read the password into a shell variable. Always pipe via `sudo -S <file`.
173	- Do **not** replace `_sudo_spawn_watchdog`'s `setsid`/`nohup` fallback with bare `setsid`. macOS has `setsid(2)` as a libc call but no `setsid(1)` CLI in base, and the backgrounded failure is silent (redirected to `/dev/null`) — every run-script then re-prompts because `_sudo_state_valid`'s `kill -0` probe finds a dead PID. See [`pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md`](pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md).
174	
175	Adding a new sudo surface in a run-script:
176	
177	1. `{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}` near the top of the template.
178	2. Set the `NEED_SUDO` template flag (mirror existing run-scripts).
179	3. Call `sudo_session_init "yourlabel"`; branch on return code + `sudo_session_skip_reason`.
180	4. Run privileged commands via `sudo_run …` (simple cases) or pass `-e @$CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE` to ansible.
181	
182	Full helper API, runtime state, cleanup model: [docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md).
183	
184	**Non-interactive password injection** (used by `scripts/fleet_apply.py` over
185	SSH): `sudo_session_init` adopts `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (a 0600 file
186	path) instead of prompting on `/dev/tty`. The helper validates with `sudo -S
187	-v -p ''` and writes into the same shared state dir, so downstream
188	run-scripts see the cached state and never re-prompt. Do **not** read
189	`CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` from your run-script directly — always go
190	through `sudo_session_init`. See [docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md)
191	→ "Non-interactive password injection" and [docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md)
192	for the orchestrator side.
193	
194	### fleet-apply semantics (counter-intuitive defaults)
195	
196	A few `just fleet-apply*` behaviours WILL trip up agents who don't know them. Full docs in [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md); the load-bearing invariants:
197	
198	- **`drift` ≠ `failed`**. When chezmoi can't prompt to overwrite a hand-edited file (no PTY over SSH), the host is shown as yellow ⚠ `drift` in the live table and the per-file paths are listed, but it does **not** count toward the exit code. Don't "fix" drift hosts unless the user asks. Resolution: hand-fix the remote, or `--force` to let the template win.
199	- **`fleet-apply-file PATH` skips `run_*` scripts**. Uses `chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts <PATH>` after an explicit `git pull`. Means ansible / Brewfile changes will NOT execute. If you edit `dot_ansible/...` and test with `fleet-apply-file`, the change won't apply — use full `fleet-apply` for ansible iterations. Same applies to Brewfile.
200	- **`--branch BRANCH` is no-op on local hosts**. The local source dir IS the user's editor working tree; switching it would be hostile. Local hosts log a warning and run against the working tree as-is. The flag also forces mode to `apply` (since `chezmoi update` would re-pull main and undo the checkout).
201	- **Install-only by design**. fleet-apply inherits the [Install vs upgrade is split](#install-vs-upgrade-is-split-on-purpose) invariant: it never silently bumps tools. The explicit upgrade path is `just upgrade-*` which must be run on each host (fleet-apply does NOT broadcast upgrades).
202	- **Process substitution + sentinel are load-bearing**. `> >(tee -a $log) 2>&1 & _cz_pid=$!; wait $_cz_pid; _rc=$?; echo $_rc > $sentinel` is the contract that `--status` / `--tail` / `--watch` rely on. Don't change to a pipeline (`| tee`) — the wrapper's SIGHUP trap depends on `$_cz_pid` pointing to chezmoi, not tee. See [docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md → Killing orphans, checking status, re-attaching](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md#killing-orphans-checking-status-re-attaching).
203	- **Conservative drift classifier**. `_classify_drift()` only downgrades stderr lines matching the exact `chezmoi: <path>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty:` fingerprint. Any unrecognised stderr line keeps `failed` state. Don't broaden the regex without explicit user request — silent downgrades hide real errors.
204	
205	### `modify_` and `create_` prefix semantics
206	
207	Two chezmoi source prefixes tame files that would otherwise churn on every apply:
208	
209	- **`modify_`** files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes current target contents into stdin, expects new contents on stdout. Used for `~/.claude/settings.json` (jq overlay), the editor `settings.json` files (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity), and the coding-agent CLI configs (`~/.cursor/cli-config.json`, `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`). Do **not** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it would overwrite your script with the live file.
210	- **`create_`** files seed once, then chezmoi never touches the contents. Used for `~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json` and editor `keybindings.json`. To refresh a `create_` baseline, copy the live file directly into the source path: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"`. Neither `chezmoi add` (strips the prefix) nor `chezmoi re-add` (silently skips) is correct.
211	
212	Full case studies (`dot_claude/modify_settings.json`, `.chezmoitemplates/editor/*`, `dot_config/nvim/create_lazy-lock.json`, `dot_codex/modify_config.toml`), failure modes, presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: [docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md → Case studies in this repo](docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md#case-studies-in-this-repo). For the three coding-agent CLI overlays specifically, the deep-dive lives at [docs/tools/agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md) (overlay key rationale, what's intentionally NOT managed and why, OpenCode legacy `config.json` migration, Codex `[projects]`/`[marketplaces.*]` round-trip, **and the Claude hook-aware merger that lets our overlay coexist with [CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland)'s auto-installed hook entries on macOS** without ping-ponging on every apply).
213	
214	### Tmux ≥ 3.3 required for popup menu, and menu must fit terminal height
215	
216	The popup menu is bound to **both** `prefix + Space` and `prefix + e` (alias) and is **generated by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`**, not defined inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two unrelated tmux quirks force this:
217	
218	1. **Position clamping (tmux ≥ 3.3 required)**: `display-menu -x R -y P` places the menu past the terminal edge on tmux 3.2a (Ubuntu 22.04 apt) and silently suppresses it. tmux 3.3+ clamps the position. The Ansible `devtools` role detects old tmux on Debian/Ubuntu and upgrades automatically (Linuxbrew when present, otherwise user-level [`nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage`](https://github.com/nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage) extracted to `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/` with a shim at `~/.local/bin/tmux`). After the upgrade, run `tmux kill-server` once — running servers keep the old binary in memory.
219	2. **Menu-too-tall silent failure (all tmux versions)**: `display-menu` does **not** paginate. If the menu is taller than the terminal (after status bar + `-y` anchor offset), the entire popup is suppressed with no error, no log entry, nothing in `tmux show-messages`. `man tmux`: _"If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."_ This was misdiagnosed for hours as a `csi-u` / `extended-keys` keysym encoding bug after a 50-row flat menu started failing on smaller terminal heights — the keys (`Space` then `Enter` then `e`) were all bound correctly the whole time.
220	
221	Hard rules when touching the popup menu:
222	
223	- **Top menu cap is ~14 rows.** Adding a 15th row will start failing on smaller heights (mobile SSH, half-screen splits). Push lower-frequency items into the appropriate submenu in `~/.config/tmux/menu-<category>.sh` instead.
224	- **Submenus are separate scripts**, each `exec tmux display-menu …`. Quoting context resets per script — keeps the inline `\"` / `{` / `}` / `;` quoting disasters out of `keybindings.conf`.
225	- **Complex commands** (anything with `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, or nested fzf binds) must live in their own script (`~/.config/tmux/sesh-picker.sh`, `sesh-windows.sh`, etc.), not inline in a menu row. tmux's parser treats `{` `}` `;` as command-block delimiters / separators even inside `'…'` inside `"…"`, silently aborting parse.
226	- **Test by shrinking the terminal vertically.** Verifying on a full-height window does not catch the height-fit failure. The top menu generator reads `#{client_height}` and tier-trims; if you change the tiers, retest at heights 14 / 22 / 60.
227	
228	See `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md` for the full debugging story (red herrings included). Adjacent pitfall: `pitfalls/yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md`.
229	
230	### Key tmux settings for coding agents
231	
232	These are non-obvious settings that other tools depend on; do not remove without checking:
233	
234	- `extended-keys always` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` — forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter through tmux to inner apps (Claude Code, Neovim, etc.)
235	- `escape-time 0` — eliminates ESC delay for Neovim
236	- `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features …:clipboard` (for `xterm*`, `ghostty*`, `alacritty*`) — OSC 52 over SSH without terminfo `Ms`. Paired with SSH-conditional `vim.g.clipboard = vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` in `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. See [docs/tools/tmux/README.md](docs/tools/tmux/README.md) → "OSC 52 Clipboard".
237	- `allow-passthrough on` — OSC passthrough for terminal images
238	- macOS terminals must send Option as Meta/Esc+ for `M-` keybindings (theme switching, layouts, fine resize). Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` (managed in `dot_config/ghostty/config`). See [docs/tools/ghostty.md](docs/tools/ghostty.md).
239	
240	Full tmux config breakdown, theme switching, keybindings table, troubleshooting: [docs/tools/tmux/](docs/tools/tmux/).
241	
242	### Zellij `default_mode "locked"`
243	
244	`dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` uses `default_mode "locked"` so all keys pass through to inner applications by default. Press `Ctrl+G` to unlock Zellij commands. This prevents key conflicts with coding agents and vim-style applications. On first Zellij launch (without existing config), select the "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" keybinding preset.
245

## Report: `tmrun` Implementation Guide

### 1. Helper Function Signatures & Behavior

| `_sesh_attach_or_switch` | `_sesh_attach_or_switch <session>` | session name | — | Inside tmux: `tmux switch-client`; outside: `tmux attach-session` (lines 62–66) |
| `_sesh_ensure_session` | `_sesh_ensure_session <session> <path>` | session name + working dir path | 0 if exists, 1 if newly created | Creates detached session if missing via `tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$target"` (lines 72–79) |
| `_sesh_wrap_agent` | `_sesh_wrap_agent <agent> [specstory_mode]` | agent name + optional mode (`auto`/`never`) | wrapped command string | For known specstory providers (claude/codex/cursor/droid/gemini) wraps in `specstory run <agent>`; others pass raw (lines 92–115) |
| `_sesh_on_exit_wrap` | `_sesh_on_exit_wrap <inner_cmd> <mode> [label]` | inner command + mode (`shell`/`kill`/`restart`) + label | wrapped shell command (single string) | Wraps with `trap '' INT` and exit handler; shell mode (default) drops to shell with hint; restart mode loops with respawn (lines 130–155) |

### 2. Autoname Pattern: Path → Session Name

From `sesh-here` (lines 189) and `sesh-root` / `sesh-code` / `sesh-vibe`:

```zsh
# sesh-here pattern (line 189):
session=$(_sesh_sanitize "$(basename "$target")")

# sesh-code pattern (lines 330–332):
repo_name=$(basename "$repo_root")
session=$(_sesh_sanitize "coding-agent/${repo_name}")

# sesh-vibe pattern (lines 586–588):
repo_name=$(basename "$repo_root")
session=$(_sesh_sanitize "vibe/${repo_name}")
```

**Pattern for `tmrun`**: `_sesh_sanitize "$(basename "$PWD")"` for a simple auto-derived name, or parameterize like scode/svibe for a prefix-based pattern.

### 3. Exact `tmux new-session -d` Invocations

**sesh-code** (line 356): Creates editor window with named pane
```zsh
tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$repo_root" -n editor "$nvim_cmd"
```

**sesh-vibe** (lines 608–609): Creates agents window with first pane command
```zsh
tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$repo_root" -n agents \
    "$(_vibe_agent_cmd "${agents[1]}")"
```

**Key patterns**:
- `-d` (detached), `-s <session_name>`, `-c <working_dir>` (all mandatory for your use case)
- `-n <window_name>` (optional; if omitted, default window is `0`)
- Command string at the end is **unquoted in the tmux invocation** (variable expansion happens in the caller)
- The wrapped command (`$nvim_cmd`, `$agent_cmd`, etc.) is already a fully-formed shell string (see `_sesh_on_exit_wrap` return); passed bare to tmux

**For `tmrun` with `$@` passthrough**: you'd want something like:
```zsh
tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$PWD" "$@"
```
(If you want to wrap the command similarly to scode/svibe, build it first with `_sesh_on_exit_wrap` then pass the result.)

 `./dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh`

```text
1	# tmux + OSC 133 capture helpers — shell-level counterparts of the
2	# prefix + M-y / M-i tmux bindings, with an N-back index.
3	#
4	#   cpcmd [N]    last (or Nth-latest) command's INPUT  (zsh history; universal)
5	#   cpout [N]    last (or Nth-latest) command's OUTPUT (tmux copy-mode chain)
6	#   cpblock [N]  last (or Nth-latest) command's FULL BLOCK, Warp-style
7	#
8	# N defaults to 1 (= latest). N=2 is the one before that, and so on.
9	#
10	# Each prints captured text to stdout (pipe-friendly: `cpout | grep ERROR`)
11	# AND copies to system clipboard. Diagnostic + byte count go to stderr so
12	# stdout stays clean for pipes.
13	#
14	# WHY cpout/cpblock need tmux:
15	# tmux consumes OSC 133 marker bytes and only stores them as per-line
16	# attributes in its grid — `tmux capture-pane -pe` does NOT re-emit them.
17	# Outside tmux there's no portable way to recover boundaries of a past
18	# command's output (terminals like iTerm2/Ghostty have proprietary APIs,
19	# but nothing cross-terminal). cpcmd uses zsh shell history instead, so it
20	# works universally.
21	#
22	# Requires: zsh; plus tmux for cpout/cpblock.
23	
24	# Pipe stdin to system clipboard, preferring tmux's OSC 52 bridge (SSH-safe)
25	# and falling back to platform-native clipboard tools.
26	_cpx_to_clipboard() {
27	  if [[ -n "$TMUX" ]]; then
28	    tmux load-buffer -w -
29	  elif command -v pbcopy &>/dev/null; then
30	    pbcopy
31	  elif command -v wl-copy &>/dev/null; then
32	    wl-copy
33	  elif command -v xclip &>/dev/null; then
34	    xclip -selection clipboard -in
35	  elif command -v xsel &>/dev/null; then
36	    xsel --clipboard --input
37	  else
38	    cat >/dev/null
39	    return 1
40	  fi
41	}
42	
43	# Validate a positive-integer argument. Echoes the value on success; prints
44	# a usage hint to stderr and returns 1 on invalid input.
45	_cpx_parse_n() {
46	  local name=$1 n=${2:-1}
47	  if [[ ! "$n" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( n < 1 )); then
48	    print -u2 "$name: N must be a positive integer (got: $n). Usage: $name [N]"
49	    return 1
50	  fi
```

```text
| Tool | Config file | Conflict risk |
|------|-------------|---------------|
| tmux (root-table) | `dot_config/tmux/keybindings.conf` | `C-h/j/k/l` (vim-tmux-navigator), `C-1..9` (window switch); `prefix + a` (live agent panes picker — `tv agent-panes`, see [docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md](docs/tools/agent-panes-discovery.md)) |
| Television (global) | `dot_config/television/config.toml` | `Ctrl+S/F/R/Y/T/X/O` (built-in actions) |
| Television (channels) | `dot_config/television/cable/*.toml` | Per-channel `[keybindings]` overrides global |
| Zellij | `dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` | Mitigated by `default_mode "locked"` |
| Ghostty | `dot_config/ghostty/config` | `macos-option-as-alt` affects `Alt+` availability |
| zsh ZLE widgets | `dot_config/zsh/tools/{11_tools_picker,12_television,22_sesh,05_aisuggest}.zsh` | `Alt+T/R/P/G/E/A/I/S` (pickers), `Alt+;` (aisuggest, configurable via `AISUGGEST_KEY`); rebound from `zvm_after_init` in `dot_zshrc.tmpl` to survive zsh-vi-mode's keybind wipe |
| Claude Code (TUI) | `dot_claude/modify_keybindings.json` (overlay) + `~/.claude/keybindings.json` (live); see [docs/tools/claude-code-keybindings.md](docs/tools/claude-code-keybindings.md) | `Ctrl+R` (history:search — collides with atuin / zsh-history-substring at the prompt outside Claude), `Ctrl+T` (toggleTodos — Television's `Ctrl+T` is shadowed when Claude has focus), `Ctrl+G` (chat:externalEditor), `Ctrl+S` (chat:stash), `Shift+Tab` (chat:cycleMode — only known mode-switch action, no jump-to-plan) |

Known conflict zones: `Ctrl+H/J/K/L` (tmux vim-tmux-navigator; removed in TV global), `Ctrl+S/F/R` (TV built-in cycling/reload — avoid in channel actions), `Alt+*` (safe namespace for channel-specific actions; requires terminal to send Option as Meta). Free Alt slots in this repo: `Alt+/`, `Alt+\`, and most letters not listed above (B/D/F/H/J/K/L/M/N/O/Q/U/V/W/X/Y/Z) — but check `dot_config/zsh/tools/*.zsh` first before claiming a new one.
--
- `allow-passthrough on` — OSC passthrough for terminal images
- macOS terminals must send Option as Meta/Esc+ for `M-` keybindings (theme switching, layouts, fine resize). Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` (managed in `dot_config/ghostty/config`). See [docs/tools/ghostty.md](docs/tools/ghostty.md).

Full tmux config breakdown, theme switching, keybindings table, troubleshooting: [docs/tools/tmux/](docs/tools/tmux/).

### Zellij `default_mode "locked"`

`dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` uses `default_mode "locked"` so all keys pass through to inner applications by default. Press `Ctrl+G` to unlock Zellij commands. This prevents key conflicts with coding agents and vim-style applications. On first Zellij launch (without existing config), select the "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" keybinding preset.

32	            --preview-window 'right:55%' \
