43	# All helpers below take care to avoid the lowercase `path` / `cdpath` /
44	# `manpath` / `fpath` zsh-tied-array trap (see
45	# pitfalls/zsh-tied-array-path-shadowing.md).
46	
47	# Resolve the git repo root, or return non-zero if not in a repo.
48	function _sesh_git_root() {
49	    git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null
50	}
51	
52	# Sanitize a string for use as a tmux session name.
53	# tmux forbids `.` and `:` in session names; we also strip whitespace.
54	function _sesh_sanitize() {
55	    print -r -- "${1//[.:[:space:]]/-}"
56	}
57	
58	# Switch to or attach to a tmux session named $1 (creating it at $2 if needed).
59	# Inside tmux: `switch-client`. Outside tmux: `attach-session`.
60	function _sesh_attach_or_switch() {
61	    local session="$1"
62	    if [[ -n "$TMUX" ]]; then
63	        tmux switch-client -t "$session"
64	    else
65	        tmux attach-session -t "$session"
66	    fi
67	}
68	
69	# Create (or no-op if exists) a detached tmux session at the given path.
70	# Returns 0 if the session already existed, 1 if newly created. (Caller uses
71	# this to decide whether to apply layout setup or just attach.)
72	function _sesh_ensure_session() {
73	    local session="$1" target="$2"
74	    if tmux has-session -t "=$session" 2>/dev/null; then
75	        return 0   # already exists
76	    fi
77	    tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$target"
78	    return 1       # newly created
79	}
80	
81	# Wrap a known specstory provider in `specstory run X` so the agent picks up
82	# auto-save markdown logging. Bare CLI names that aren't specstory providers
83	# (currently: opencode — see backlog/specstory-opencode-support.md) pass
84	# through unchanged.
85	#
86	# Update the case list when specstory adds providers (track upstream:
87	# specstoryai/getspecstory#146 for opencode, similar issues for others).
88	#
89	# Args: $1=agent, $2=specstory_mode (auto|never; default auto)
90	#   auto  — wrap if known provider, raw otherwise (the historical default)
91	#   never — pass through raw regardless (CLI flag --no-specstory sets this)
92	function _sesh_wrap_agent() {
93	    local agent="$1" specstory_mode="${2:-auto}"
94	    if [[ "$specstory_mode" == "never" ]]; then
95	        # Even an empty agent goes raw → caller's responsibility to pick a
96	        # sensible default (we choose `claude` upstream when --no-specstory
97	        # is set, since `specstory run` with no arg defaults to claude too).
98	        print -r -- "${agent:-claude}"
99	        return
100	    fi
101	    case "$agent" in
102	        ""|"specstory")
103	            # No agent specified → bare `specstory run` (default = claude).
104	            print -r -- "specstory run"
105	            ;;
106	        claude|codex|cursor|droid|gemini)
107	            print -r -- "specstory run $agent"
108	            ;;
109	        *)
110	            # Pass-through for non-specstory providers (opencode today, more
111	            # later as specstory adds support).
112	            print -r -- "$agent"
113	            ;;
114	    esac
115	}
116	
117	# Build a wrapper command that controls what happens when the inner command
118	# exits (Ctrl+C, agent quit, crash). `--on-exit shell|kill|restart`:
119	#   shell   — print a hint, then drop into $SHELL so user can restart agent,
120	#             switch to lazygit, kill the pane manually, etc. (default)
121	#   kill    — let the pane close on exit (tmux default `remain-on-exit off`)
122	#   restart — wrap in `while true; do CMD; sleep 1; done` so the agent
123	#             auto-respawns. Use Ctrl+C twice quickly to break the loop and
124	#             land in shell.
125	#
126	# Args: $1=inner_cmd, $2=mode, $3=label_for_hint
127	# Stdout: the wrapped shell command (single string suitable for `tmux
128	# new-window … "<cmd>"`). Quoting is structured so user $SHELL is the one
129	# evaluating the inner command — we don't double-eval.
130	function _sesh_on_exit_wrap() {
131	    local inner="$1" mode="$2" label="${3:-agent}"
132	    # Ctrl+C sends SIGINT to the entire foreground process group, so the
133	    # wrapper shell itself dies before it can print the hint or exec the
134	    # login shell — the pane just vanishes. `trap '' INT` makes the wrapper
135	    # ignore SIGINT; the inner command still receives it and exits normally,
136	    # then control returns to the wrapper which prints the hint as intended.
137	    # (Tools that install their own SIGINT handler — btop, htop, less — were
138	    # the visible failure case; agent CLIs happened to handle Ctrl+C as
139	    # clean exit so this was masked for them.)
140	    local guard="trap '' INT;"
141	    case "$mode" in
142	        kill)
143	            print -r -- "$inner"
144	            ;;
145	        restart)
146	            # `|| true` so a crash exit doesn't abort the loop on `set -e` shells
147	            print -r -- "$guard while true; do $inner || true; echo '[$label exited — respawning in 1s; Ctrl+C twice to break]'; sleep 1; done; exec \$SHELL -l"
148	            ;;
149	        shell|*)
150	            # Default. Hint message uses tmux color codes — works in all
151	            # terminals tmux supports.
152	            print -r -- "$guard $inner; printf '\\n\\033[33m[$label exited — back in shell. Re-run with: \\033[1m%s\\033[0;33m]\\033[0m\\n' \"$inner\"; exec \$SHELL -l"
153	            ;;
154	    esac
155	}
156	
157	# Connect to a sesh session for the current directory (creates it if missing).
158	# Lightweight: drops you into a plain shell at $PWD with NO startup command.
159	# For an editor-first session use `scode` (repo-aware, full layout) or just
160	# launch nvim manually inside the new session.
161	#
162	# Smart argument handling:
163	#   shere                              # plain shell at $PWD, no command
164	#   shere specstory run codex          # bare args → treated as command
165	#   shere -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
166	#   shere -p ~/my-proj                 # explicit path, plain shell
167	#   shere -p ~/my-proj npm run dev     # explicit path + command
168	function sesh-here() {
169	    local cmd="" target=""
170	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
171	        case "$1" in
172	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
173	            -p|--path)    target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
174	            -*)           echo "sesh-here: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
175	            *)            break ;;  # remaining args are the command
176	        esac
177	    done
178	    [[ $# -gt 0 && -z "$cmd" ]] && cmd="$*"
179	    target="${target:-$PWD}"
180	    if [[ -n "$cmd" ]]; then
181	        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$target"
182	    else
183	        # Bypass sesh's default_session.startup_command (nvim) for a plain
184	        # shell. We create the session via tmux directly, then attach. This
185	        # also means the wildcard startup_command (project layout) is
186	        # bypassed — `shere` is intentionally lightweight; use `scode`,
187	        # `svibe`, or `sesh connect <path>` for layouts.
188	        local session
189	        session=$(_sesh_sanitize "$(basename "$target")")
190	        _sesh_ensure_session "$session" "$target"
191	        _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
192	    fi
193	}
194	
195	# Connect to the current git root when available, otherwise use $PWD.
196	# Same smart argument handling as sesh-here.
197	#   sroot                              # default startup_command
198	#   sroot specstory run codex          # bare args → command
199	#   sroot -c "specstory run codex"     # explicit --command flag
200	function sesh-root() {
201	    local cmd="" root
202	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
203	        case "$1" in
204	            -c|--command) cmd="$2"; shift 2 ;;
205	            -*)           shift ;;
206	            *)            break ;;
207	        esac
208	    done
209	    [[ $# -gt 0 && -z "$cmd" ]] && cmd="$*"
210	    root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) || root=$PWD
211	    if [[ -n "$cmd" ]]; then
212	        sesh connect --command "$cmd" "$root"
213	    else
214	        sesh connect "$root"
215	    fi
216	}
217	
218	alias shere='sesh-here'
219	alias sroot='sesh-root'
220	alias scode='sesh-code'
221	alias svibe='sesh-vibe'
222	
223	# ── scode: repo-aware coding-agent layout ───────────────────────────────────
224	#
225	# Open the coding-agent layout (nvim 75% | specstory-wrapped agent 25%, btop
226	# window) in a session NAMED FOR THE CURRENT REPO, so different repos don't
227	# collide on the single `coding-agent` session name.
228	#
229	# Session naming:
230	#   In repo /Volumes/Data/Program/Personal/foo  → session `coding-agent/foo`
231	#   Same repo re-invocation                     → attach (no duplicate)
232	#   Different repo                              → new session `coding-agent/<other>`
233	#
234	# Outside a git repo the function refuses with a hint to use `shere` or `svibe`
235	# (the heavy layout doesn't make sense for ad-hoc directories).
236	#
237	# Agent wrapping: known specstory providers (claude/codex/cursor/droid/gemini)
238	# are auto-wrapped in `specstory run X` for markdown auto-save. Others
239	# (opencode today) pass through raw — see _sesh_wrap_agent + backlog entry
240	# `specstory-opencode-support` for the upstream tracking.
241	#
242	# Exit behavior: `--on-exit shell` (default) drops to a shell with a hint when
243	# the agent exits, so Ctrl+C doesn't kill the pane. Use `--on-exit kill` for
244	# the old behavior, or `--on-exit restart` for an auto-respawn loop.
245	#
246	# Usage:
247	#   scode                              # current repo, default agent (specstory → claude)
248	#   scode codex                        # specstory run codex
249	#   scode opencode                     # opencode raw (not yet a specstory provider)
250	#   scode --on-exit kill claude        # Ctrl+C kills the right pane
251	#   scode --on-exit restart codex      # codex auto-respawns on crash
252	#   scode -p ~/some/other/repo         # explicit repo path
253	#   scode --no-attach                  # create session in background, don't switch
254	function sesh-code() {
255	    local target="" agent="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto"
256	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
257	        case "$1" in
258	            -p|--path)      target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
259	            -a|--agent)     agent="$2"; shift 2 ;;
260	            --on-exit)      on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
261	            --no-specstory) specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
262	            --specstory)    specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
263	            --no-attach)    no_attach=1; shift ;;
264	            --agents)
265	                echo "scode: --agents is svibe-only (scode is single-agent)." >&2
266	                echo "       For multi-agent layouts: svibe --agents '$2'" >&2
267	                return 1 ;;
268	            -h|--help)
269	                cat <<'EOF'
270	scode — open repo-scoped coding-agent layout
271	
272	Usage: scode [--path DIR] [--agent CLI] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory]
273	             [--no-attach] [AGENT]
274	
275	Layout: window `editor` (nvim 75% | agent 25%) + window `monitor` (btop).
276	Session name: `coding-agent/<repo-basename>` (one session per repo).
277	Requires:     git repo (errors otherwise — use `shere` or `svibe`).
278	
279	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
280	  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
281	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
282	
283	--on-exit MODE controls what happens when ANY pane command exits/Ctrl+C
284	(applies to the agent pane, the nvim pane, and the btop monitor window):
285	  shell    (default) — drop to shell with a hint, command re-runnable
286	  kill                — let the pane/window close (tmux default)
287	  restart             — auto-respawn the command in a loop
288	
289	Examples:
290	  scode                            # current repo, default agent (specstory → claude)
291	  scode codex                      # right pane: specstory run codex
292	  scode opencode                   # right pane: opencode (raw)
293	  scode --no-specstory claude      # right pane: claude (raw, no markdown auto-save)
294	  scode --on-exit kill claude      # right pane closes when claude exits
295	  scode -p ~/work/foo              # explicit repo path
296	EOF
297	                return 0 ;;
298	            -*)             echo "scode: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
299	            *)              [[ -z "$agent" ]] && agent="$1" || true; shift ;;
300	        esac
301	    done
302	
303	    case "$on_exit" in
304	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
305	        *) echo "scode: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
306	    esac
307	
308	    # Resolve repo root
309	    local repo_root
310	    if [[ -n "$target" ]]; then
311	        repo_root=$(cd "$target" 2>/dev/null && _sesh_git_root)
312	    else
313	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
314	    fi
315	    if [[ -z "$repo_root" ]]; then
316	        echo "scode: not inside a git repo." >&2
317	        echo "       Use \`shere\` for a plain shell, or \`svibe\` for a vibe layout in any dir." >&2
318	        return 1
319	    fi
320	
321	    # Validate agent CLI exists in PATH (fail-fast). Specstory itself isn't
322	    # checked here — if the user passed a known provider but specstory is
323	    # missing, the pane will exit with specstory's error message and
324	    # --on-exit=shell will leave a shell to read it.
325	    if [[ -n "$agent" ]] && ! command -v "$agent" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
326	        echo "scode: agent CLI '$agent' not found in PATH." >&2
327	        return 1
328	    fi
329	
330	    local repo_name session
331	    repo_name=$(basename "$repo_root")
332	    session=$(_sesh_sanitize "coding-agent/${repo_name}")
333	
334	    # If session already exists, just attach (idempotent — solves the
335	    # cross-repo collision problem the old single `coding-agent` session had).
336	    if tmux has-session -t "=$session" 2>/dev/null; then
337	        (( no_attach )) || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
338	        return 0
339	    fi
340	
341	    # Create session + build layout directly with tmux commands (see svibe
342	    # comment block for why not tmuxp).
343	    #
344	    # Window 1 "editor": nvim (left, will be 75%) | wrapped agent (right, 25%)
345	    # Window 2 "monitor": btop (or htop / top fallback)
346	    local agent_inner agent_cmd
347	    agent_inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$agent" "$specstory_mode")
348	    agent_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$agent_inner" "$on_exit" "${agent:-agent}")
349	
350	    # nvim and monitor get the same on-exit treatment as the agent so that
351	    # quitting them drops to a shell with a re-launch hint instead of the
352	    # pane/window vanishing.
353	    local nvim_cmd monitor_inner monitor_cmd
354	    nvim_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")
355	
356	    tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$repo_root" -n editor "$nvim_cmd"
357	    tmux split-window -h -t "${session}:editor" -c "$repo_root" "$agent_cmd"
358	    # main-vertical layout, then size the LEFT pane to 75% of window width
359	    tmux select-layout -t "${session}:editor" main-vertical >/dev/null
360	    tmux resize-pane -t "${session}:editor.1" -x 75% 2>/dev/null
361	
362	    # Monitor window
363	    if   command -v btop >/dev/null 2>&1; then monitor_inner=btop
364	    elif command -v htop >/dev/null 2>&1; then monitor_inner=htop
365	    else                                       monitor_inner=top
366	    fi
367	    monitor_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "$monitor_inner" "$on_exit" "$monitor_inner")
368	    tmux new-window -t "$session" -n monitor -c "$repo_root" "$monitor_cmd"
369	
370	    # Focus editor window, left (nvim) pane
371	    tmux select-window -t "${session}:editor"
372	    tmux select-pane -t "${session}:editor.1"
373	
374	    (( no_attach )) || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
375	}
376	
377	# ── svibe: parametric multi-agent vibe layout ───────────────────────────────
378	#
379	# A "vibe coding" session: window 1 has N agent panes (default 4), window 2
380	# is lazygit, window 3 is nvim. Built directly with tmux split/new-window
381	# commands so it stays parametric (tmuxp YAML can't express dynamic pane counts).
382	#
383	# Session naming: `vibe/<dir-basename>` — collision-safe across directories.
384	# Refuses outside a git repo (use `shere` for plain shells in arbitrary dirs).
385	#
386	# Each agent pane is wrapped in `specstory run X` (for known providers, opt
387	# out with --no-specstory) and additionally wrapped in an exit handler
388	# controlled by `--on-exit MODE` — same semantics as `scode`. Default `shell`
389	# keeps the pane open with a hint after the agent exits, so Ctrl+C is
390	# recoverable.
391	#
392	# Two modes for choosing which agents run:
393	#   1. Homogeneous (positional): `svibe 4 codex` → 4 panes all running codex
394	#   2. Heterogeneous (--agents):  `svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode`
395	#                                 → 4 panes running those specific agents
396	#                                 (list LENGTH determines pane count;
397	#                                 positional N_AGENTS is rejected to avoid
398	#                                 ambiguity)
399	#
400	# Usage:
401	#   svibe                                          # 4× claude (specstory)
402	#   svibe 2                                        # 2× claude
403	#   svibe 4 codex                                  # 4× specstory run codex
404	#   svibe 3 opencode                               # 3× opencode (raw)
405	#   svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode     # 4 panes, mixed
406	#   svibe --agents claude,opencode --on-exit kill  # 2 panes, mixed, hard exit
407	#   svibe --no-specstory 4 claude                  # 4× claude (raw, no md auto-save)
408	#   svibe --on-exit restart 4 codex                # auto-respawn loop
409	#   svibe -p ~/repo 4 claude                       # explicit path
410	#   svibe --no-attach 4 claude                     # create in background
411	function sesh-vibe() {
412	    local target="" no_attach=0 on_exit="shell" specstory_mode="auto"
413	    local n_agents=4 n_agents_set=0
414	    local agent_cli="claude"
415	    local agents_csv=""
416	    local min_width="${SVIBE_MIN_WIDTH:-80}"
417	    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
418	        case "$1" in
419	            -p|--path)      target="$2"; shift 2 ;;
420	            --on-exit)      on_exit="$2"; shift 2 ;;
421	            --agents)       agents_csv="$2"; shift 2 ;;
422	            --min-width)    min_width="$2"; shift 2 ;;
423	            --no-specstory) specstory_mode="never"; shift ;;
424	            --specstory)    specstory_mode="auto"; shift ;;
425	            --no-attach)    no_attach=1; shift ;;
426	            -h|--help)
427	                cat <<'EOF'
428	svibe — parametric multi-agent vibe layout
429	
430	Usage:
431	  svibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
432	        [--min-width COLS] [N_AGENTS] [AGENT_CLI]
433	  svibe [--path DIR] [--on-exit MODE] [--no-specstory] [--no-attach]
434	        [--min-width COLS] --agents A1,A2,A3[,...]
435	
436	Default: svibe           (N auto-picked from term_width ÷ min-width, clamp [1,12])
437	  window 1 "agents" — N agent panes (columns if all fit at ≥min-width, else tiled)
438	  window 2 "git"    — lazygit
439	  window 3 "edit"   — nvim
440	
441	Two modes for choosing agents:
442	  Homogeneous:    `svibe 4 codex` → 4 panes all codex
443	  Heterogeneous:  `svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode`
444	                  → 4 panes (one each, in order); list length = pane count
445	
446	Session name: `vibe/<repo-basename>` (collision-safe per directory).
447	Requires:     git repo (use `shere` for plain shells elsewhere).
448	
449	Agent wrapping (auto, opt out with --no-specstory):
450	  claude / codex / cursor / droid / gemini  → `specstory run <agent>`
451	  opencode (and other unknown CLIs)         → raw passthrough
452	
453	--on-exit MODE controls per-pane behavior on Ctrl+C / clean exit
454	(applies to all agent panes, the lazygit window, and the nvim window):
455	  shell    (default) — drop to shell with a hint, command re-runnable
456	  kill                — let the pane/window close (tmux default)
457	  restart             — auto-respawn the command in a loop
458	
459	--min-width COLS sets the minimum readable per-pane width (default: value of
460	$SVIBE_MIN_WIDTH, else 80). It drives two decisions:
461	  • auto-pick N when you don't pass a count (N = term_width / min-width)
462	  • columns vs tiled in the agents window: columns when all N panes fit at
463	    ≥COLS wide side-by-side, otherwise tiled grid
464	Example on a 240-col terminal:
465	  min-width 80   → auto N=3, three even-horizontal columns
466	  min-width 120  → auto N=2, two even-horizontal columns
467	
468	Examples:
469	  svibe                                            # auto N × claude, width-aware layout
470	  svibe 2                                          # 2× claude
471	  svibe 4 codex                                    # 4× codex
472	  svibe 6 opencode                                 # 6× opencode (heavy)
473	  svibe --min-width 120                            # wider panes → fewer auto columns
474	  svibe --agents claude,codex,codex,opencode       # 4 panes, mixed
475	  svibe --agents claude,opencode --on-exit kill    # 2 panes, mixed
476	  svibe --no-specstory 4 claude                    # raw claude, no auto-save
477	EOF
478	                return 0 ;;
479	            -*)             echo "svibe: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 1 ;;
480	            *)              break ;;
481	        esac
482	    done
483	
484	    if ! [[ "$min_width" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || (( min_width < 1 )); then
485	        echo "svibe: --min-width must be a positive integer (got: $min_width)" >&2
486	        return 1
487	    fi
488	
489	    # Current terminal width, used for auto-picking N (when the user didn't
490	    # pass a count) and for the columns-vs-tiled cutover. $COLUMNS is
491	    # auto-maintained by zsh on SIGWINCH; tput is a fallback for corner cases
492	    # (e.g. non-interactive invocation); 200 is a generous last resort.
493	    local term_width="${COLUMNS:-$(tput cols 2>/dev/null || echo 200)}"
494	
495	    # Build the agents array. Two paths:
496	    #   --agents claude,codex,…  → split csv, list length = pane count
497	    #   positional [N] [CLI]     → repeat CLI N times (N auto-picked if omitted)
498	    # Mixing both is rejected to keep semantics unambiguous.
499	    local -a agents
500	    if [[ -n "$agents_csv" ]]; then
501	        if [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
502	            echo "svibe: cannot combine --agents with positional N_AGENTS/AGENT_CLI." >&2
503	            echo "       Pick one. (e.g. drop the trailing args)" >&2
504	            return 1
505	        fi
506	        # Split CSV. Trim whitespace per element so 'claude, codex' works.
507	        local IFS=','
508	        agents=( ${=agents_csv} )
509	        # Trim leading/trailing whitespace on each element
510	        local j
511	        for (( j = 1; j <= ${#agents}; j++ )); do
512	            agents[$j]="${agents[$j]## }"
513	            agents[$j]="${agents[$j]%% }"
514	        done
515	        if (( ${#agents} == 0 )); then
516	            echo "svibe: --agents list is empty." >&2
517	            return 1
518	        fi
519	    else
520	        # Positional: [n_agents] [agent_cli]
521	        if [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; then
522	            if [[ "$1" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
523	                n_agents="$1"; n_agents_set=1; shift
524	            fi
525	        fi
526	        [[ $# -gt 0 ]] && agent_cli="$1"
527	
528	        # Auto-pick N from terminal width when the user didn't pass one.
529	        # N = clamp(term_width / min_width, 1, 12). On a 240-col terminal
530	        # with min-width 80 that's N=3; at min-width 120, N=2.
531	        if (( ! n_agents_set )); then
532	            n_agents=$(( term_width / min_width ))
533	            (( n_agents < 1 )) && n_agents=1
534	            (( n_agents > 12 )) && n_agents=12
535	        fi
536	
537	        # Build a homogeneous array of length n_agents
538	        local k
539	        for (( k = 1; k <= n_agents; k++ )); do
540	            agents+=( "$agent_cli" )
541	        done
542	    fi
543	
544	    case "$on_exit" in
545	        shell|kill|restart) ;;
546	        *) echo "svibe: --on-exit must be one of: shell, kill, restart (got: $on_exit)" >&2; return 1 ;;
547	    esac
548	
549	    if (( ${#agents} < 1 || ${#agents} > 12 )); then
550	        echo "svibe: agent count = ${#agents} out of range [1, 12]" >&2
551	        return 1
552	    fi
553	
554	    # Resolve repo root
555	    local repo_root
556	    if [[ -n "$target" ]]; then
557	        repo_root=$(cd "$target" 2>/dev/null && _sesh_git_root)
558	    else
559	        repo_root=$(_sesh_git_root)
560	    fi
561	    if [[ -z "$repo_root" ]]; then
562	        echo "svibe: not inside a git repo." >&2
563	        echo "       Use \`shere\` for a plain shell in arbitrary directories." >&2
564	        return 1
565	    fi
566	
567	    # Validate ALL agent CLIs exist in PATH (fail-fast — we don't want to
568	    # build a 4-pane layout where one pane is dead). De-dup the list to keep
569	    # the error message readable.
570	    local -a missing
571	    local -A seen
572	    local a
573	    for a in "${agents[@]}"; do
574	        [[ -n "${seen[$a]:-}" ]] && continue
575	        seen[$a]=1
576	        if ! command -v "$a" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
577	            missing+=( "$a" )
578	        fi
579	    done
580	    if (( ${#missing} > 0 )); then
581	        echo "svibe: agent CLI(s) not found in PATH: ${missing[*]}" >&2
582	        echo "       Available: $(for c in claude codex opencode cursor droid gemini; do command -v $c >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo -n "$c "; done)" >&2
583	        return 1
584	    fi
585	
586	    local repo_name session
587	    repo_name=$(basename "$repo_root")
588	    session=$(_sesh_sanitize "vibe/${repo_name}")
589	
590	    # Idempotent: existing session = just attach
591	    if tmux has-session -t "=$session" 2>/dev/null; then
592	        (( no_attach )) || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
593	        return 0
594	    fi
595	
596	    # Build wrapped command for each agent (the wrapping is pane-specific so
597	    # we can mix providers in one window).
598	    #
599	    # Helper: turn agent name → fully-wrapped tmux command string.
600	    _vibe_agent_cmd() {
601	        local inner
602	        inner=$(_sesh_wrap_agent "$1" "$specstory_mode")
603	        _sesh_on_exit_wrap "$inner" "$on_exit" "$1"
604	    }
605	
606	    # ── Build the session ───────────────────────────────────────────────
607	    # Window 1: agents (start with first pane running agents[1])
608	    tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$repo_root" -n agents \
609	        "$(_vibe_agent_cmd "${agents[1]}")"
610	
611	    # Pick window layout based on agent count vs what fits as readable
612	    # side-by-side columns at --min-width:
613	    #   N ≤ term_width / min_width → even-horizontal (columns)
614	    #   otherwise                  → tiled (grid — columns would be too narrow)
615	    local max_columns=$(( term_width / min_width ))
616	    (( max_columns < 1 )) && max_columns=1
617	    local svibe_layout
618	    if (( ${#agents} <= max_columns )); then
619	        svibe_layout="even-horizontal"
620	    else
621	        svibe_layout="tiled"
622	    fi
623	
624	    # Add remaining panes
625	    local i
626	    for (( i = 2; i <= ${#agents}; i++ )); do
627	        tmux split-window -t "${session}:agents" -c "$repo_root" \
628	            "$(_vibe_agent_cmd "${agents[$i]}")"
629	        # Re-balance after each split so layout stays uniform
630	        tmux select-layout -t "${session}:agents" "$svibe_layout" >/dev/null
631	    done
632	
633	    unset -f _vibe_agent_cmd
634	
635	    # Window 2: git (lazygit if present)
636	    # lazygit and nvim get the same on-exit handling as agents — quitting
637	    # them drops to shell with a re-launch hint rather than killing the window.
638	    local git_cmd edit_cmd
639	    if command -v lazygit >/dev/null 2>&1; then
640	        git_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "lazygit" "$on_exit" "lazygit")
641	        tmux new-window -t "$session" -n git -c "$repo_root" "$git_cmd"
642	    else
643	        # `git status; exec $SHELL` already lands in shell — no wrap needed.
644	        tmux new-window -t "$session" -n git -c "$repo_root" "git status; exec \$SHELL"
645	    fi
646	
647	    # Window 3: edit (nvim)
648	    edit_cmd=$(_sesh_on_exit_wrap "nvim" "$on_exit" "nvim")
649	    tmux new-window -t "$session" -n edit -c "$repo_root" "$edit_cmd"
650	
651	    # Focus agents window, first pane
652	    tmux select-window -t "${session}:agents"
653	    tmux select-pane -t "${session}:agents.1"
654	
655	    (( no_attach )) || _sesh_attach_or_switch "$session"
656	}
657	
658	# Register as zsh widget
659	zle -N sesh-sessions
660	
661	# Key bindings (Alt+S for session switcher, avoids conflict with Ctrl+A tmux prefix)
662	bindkey -M emacs '\es' sesh-sessions
663	bindkey -M viins '\es' sesh-sessions
664	bindkey -M vicmd '\es' sesh-sessions
665
```

### Zellij `default_mode "locked"`

`dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` uses `default_mode "locked"` so all keys pass through to inner applications by default. Press `Ctrl+G` to unlock Zellij commands. This prevents key conflicts with coding agents and vim-style applications. On first Zellij launch (without existing config), select the "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" keybinding preset.

# `mrun` design — recommended plan

## TL;DR picks

| Question | Pick | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1. File layout | **New file `dot_config/zsh/tools/23_mrun.zsh`** | Different concern from sesh (one-shot ephemeral vs. project layout). Source order > 22 still lets it call `_sesh_sanitize`. |
| 2. Function shape | **Hybrid: one `mrun` dispatcher, two pinned wrappers `tmrun` / `zjrun` as functions (not aliases)** | Single source of truth for arg parsing + name derivation; wrappers are 2-line shims that pre-set the backend. Aliases can't override `-b` cleanly. |
| 3. Signature | `mrun [-b BACKEND] [-n NAME] [-d DIR] [--no-detach] [--] CMD [ARGS...]` | Auto-name `run-$(basename PWD)-NNNN` when `-n` omitted. `--` is **optional** but recommended; everything after the first non-flag is the command. No CMD → usage + exit 2. Pass `"$@"` through, never re-join. |
| 4. Nesting | **(b) create the detached session anyway, with stderr warning** | Matches "fire and forget"; tmux/zellij handle parallel sessions cleanly. `tmux new-window` would change semantics (in-session vs new session). |
| 5. Zellij implementation | Layout KDL via heredoc + `printf %q`-equivalent escaping, **always wrap as `sh -c "$cmd"`**, spawn detached via `setsid`-with-`nohup`-fallback (mirroring `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh`). **Keep layout file** on disk — `/tmp` GC handles it. | Sub-shell wrap mirrors tmux semantics, supports pipelines/`&&`. Detach fallback is documented in-repo precedent. Layout-file lifetime: zellij re-reads it on session resurrection, so deleting risks losing the session on restart. |
| 6. Attach hint | tmux: `Started detached: tmux attach -t <name>` (or `tmux switch-client -t` if `$TMUX` set). Zellij: `Started detached: zellij attach <name>`. Single line, stderr. | Non-negotiable per user. Switch vs attach hint is the same nicety as `_sesh_attach_or_switch`. |
| 7. Aliases | **No additional aliases.** `mrun`/`tmrun`/`zjrun` are already short. | `m`/`tm`/`zj` 2-letter prefixes are too risky; `tm` collides with common tmux helpers users add later. |
| 8. Docs | Add 3 rows to `docs/zsh/aliases.md` Session Management section. **No** `docs/tools/sesh.md` cross-link (mrun is not sesh). **No** CLAUDE.md edit. | Matches existing convention (one row per public function). |
| 9. Verification | Shown below as concrete commands. | — |

## Push-backs on user's leans

**On Q1 (file layout):** Agreed — new file. One subtle point: 23_mrun.zsh must do the same `command -v tmux` / `command -v zellij` early-return dance per backend, not a single hard `return 0`. If neither is installed, the file loads no functions; if only one is installed, the dispatcher errors with a "backend X not installed" message when invoked with that backend. Don't gate the whole file on tmux+zellij both being present.

**On Q2 (shape):** Pushed back — pure aliases for `tmrun`/`zjrun` (`alias tmrun='mrun -b tmux'`) work but force the user to put `--` before NAME if they want `-n`. Better as **functions**:
```zsh
function tmrun() { mrun -b tmux  "$@"; }
function zjrun() { mrun -b zellij "$@"; }
```

**On Q4 (nesting):** Agreed with (b) but add: when `$TMUX` is set and backend=tmux, the attach hint should say `tmux switch-client -t <name>` (matches `_sesh_attach_or_switch` precedent). When `$ZELLIJ` is set and backend=zellij, zellij has no equivalent "switch" — note that the user must detach first. Single stderr line: `Note: you're already inside a $ZELLIJ session; detach (Ctrl+o d) before attach.`

**On Q5 (always wrap as `sh -c`):** Strongly agreed. Without it, `mrun -- npm test && say done` is grammatically weird (`&&` would be parsed by the outer shell, not the new pane). With wrap, the user passes one logical shell line and it Just Works on both backends. Tmux already shells out by default; we lose nothing by being explicit.

**On Q5 (layout-file lifetime):** Don't delete it. Reason: zellij's session resurrection (Ctrl+s d, then `zellij attach --session-name X`) re-reads the layout. If we `rm` it after spawn, a resurrected session loses its layout reference. Cost of leaving it: ~200 bytes per `mrun` invocation in `$TMPDIR`. Not worth the risk.

**On Q5 (KDL escaping):** KDL strings are double-quoted with `\"` and `\\` as the only escapes that matter for our case (we control the structure; only the `args` payload is user-supplied). Since we wrap as `sh -c "<full cmd>"`, the only string we need to escape is the entire command line. Use a zsh `${var//\"/\\\"}` substitution + `${var//\\/\\\\}` (in that order: backslash first, then quote — otherwise we double-escape the escaping backslashes). One regex, three lines.

**On Q7 (aliases):** Pushed back — don't add 2-letter aliases. The user's repo already has `shere`/`sroot`/`scode`/`svibe` which are 4–5 chars. `mrun`/`tmrun`/`zjrun` are already in that range. Adding `mr`/`tmr` increases collision surface for ~1 char of typing.

## Sketched function bodies

```zsh
# dot_config/zsh/tools/23_mrun.zsh
#
# mrun: fire-and-forget a command into a NEW DETACHED multiplexer session.
# Backends: tmux (default) and zellij.
#
# Usage:
#   mrun [-b tmux|zellij] [-n NAME] [-d DIR] [--no-detach] [--] CMD [ARGS...]
#   tmrun ...   # forces -b tmux
#   zjrun ...   # forces -b zellij
#
# Env override: MRUN_BACKEND=tmux|zellij (default tmux)
#
# Examples:
#   mrun -- npm run dev
#   mrun -n build -- cargo build --release
#   tmrun -- pytest -x
#   zjrun -d ~/work/foo -- ./long_running.sh
#
# Detach behavior: returns immediately. The session lives until the inner
# command exits AND you've detached from any attach. Print attach hint to
# stderr. With --no-detach, attach immediately after creation (mostly for
# debugging the helper itself).

# Soft early-return: at least one backend must be available
if ! command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! command -v zellij >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    return 0
fi

# Auto-name: run-<dir>-<rand4>. <dir> is sanitized; <rand4> avoids collisions
# when the same dir gets multiple runs in flight.
function _mrun_default_name() {
    local base
    base=$(_sesh_sanitize "$(basename "$PWD")")
    printf 'run-%s-%04x\n' "$base" $((RANDOM % 65536))
}

# Detach a backgrounded command from the current shell, surviving shell exit.
# Mirrors scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh:_sudo_spawn_watchdog (setsid → nohup
# fallback). See pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md.
function _mrun_spawn_detached() {
    # "$@" = full argv to exec
    if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        setsid "$@" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
    else
        nohup "$@" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
    fi
    disown 2>/dev/null || true
}

# KDL-escape a string for embedding inside a "..."-quoted KDL value.
# Order matters: backslashes first, then double-quotes.
function _mrun_kdl_escape() {
    local s="$1"
    s="${s//\\/\\\\}"
    s="${s//\"/\\\"}"
    print -r -- "$s"
}

# Backend: tmux. Creates detached session running CMD via the user's $SHELL.
function _mrun_tmux() {
    local session="$1" workdir="$2" no_detach="$3"; shift 3
    if tmux has-session -t "=$session" 2>/dev/null; then
        echo "mrun: tmux session '$session' already exists; pick a different -n NAME." >&2
        return 1
    fi
    # tmux new-session takes a single SHELL-CMD string. We hand it sh -c with
    # the original argv joined safely via printf %q (zsh's q flag).
    local quoted
    quoted=$(printf '%q ' "$@")
    tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$workdir" -n run \
        "sh -c ${(q)quoted}"
    if [[ -n "$TMUX" ]]; then
        echo "mrun[tmux]: started '$session'. Attach: tmux switch-client -t $session" >&2
    else
        echo "mrun[tmux]: started '$session'. Attach: tmux attach -t $session" >&2
    fi
    if (( no_detach )); then
        if [[ -n "$TMUX" ]]; then tmux switch-client -t "$session"
        else tmux attach -t "$session"
        fi
    fi
}

# Backend: zellij. Generates an ephemeral KDL layout, spawns zellij detached.
function _mrun_zellij() {
    local session="$1" workdir="$2" no_detach="$3"; shift 3
    if zellij list-sessions 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $1}' | grep -qx "$session"; then
        echo "mrun: zellij session '$session' already exists; pick a different -n NAME." >&2
        return 1
    fi
    # Build the shell line. We wrap in `sh -c` so users can pass pipelines,
    # &&, env=val prefixes, etc. — same semantics as the tmux backend.
    local cmdline esc_cmd esc_dir
    cmdline=$(printf '%q ' "$@")
    esc_cmd=$(_mrun_kdl_escape "$cmdline")
    esc_dir=$(_mrun_kdl_escape "$workdir")

    local layout
    layout=$(mktemp -t mrun-layout-XXXXXX) || return 1
    # NOTE: we do NOT rm $layout. zellij re-reads it on session resurrection;
    # /tmp GC handles the leak. ~200 bytes per run.
    cat >"$layout" <<EOF
layout {
    tab name="run" {
        pane cwd="$esc_dir" {
            command "sh"
            args "-c" "$esc_cmd"
        }
    }
}
EOF
    if [[ -n "$ZELLIJ" ]]; then
        echo "mrun[zellij]: warning — already inside zellij session '$ZELLIJ'." >&2
        echo "             The new session '$session' will run in parallel; detach (Ctrl+o d) to attach it." >&2
    fi
    if (( no_detach )); then
        zellij --layout "$layout" attach --create "$session"
    else
        _mrun_spawn_detached zellij --layout "$layout" attach --create "$session"
        echo "mrun[zellij]: started '$session'. Attach: zellij attach $session" >&2
    fi
}

# Public dispatcher.
function mrun() {
    local backend="${MRUN_BACKEND:-tmux}" name="" workdir="$PWD" no_detach=0
    while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
        case "$1" in
            -b|--backend) backend="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            -n|--name)    name="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            -d|--dir)     workdir="$2"; shift 2 ;;
            --no-detach)  no_detach=1; shift ;;
            --)           shift; break ;;
            -h|--help)
                cat <<'EOF'
mrun — fire a command into a detached tmux/zellij session

Usage: mrun [-b tmux|zellij] [-n NAME] [-d DIR] [--no-detach] [--] CMD [ARGS...]

  -b BACKEND   tmux (default) or zellij. Override via $MRUN_BACKEND.
  -n NAME      session name (default: run-<dir>-<rand>)
  -d DIR       working directory for the inner command (default: $PWD)
  --no-detach  attach immediately after creating (debug)
  --           explicit end of mrun flags; everything after is the command

Pinned wrappers: tmrun (forces tmux), zjrun (forces zellij).
EOF
                return 0 ;;
            -*) echo "mrun: unknown flag $1" >&2; return 2 ;;
            *)  break ;;
        esac
    done

    if (( $# == 0 )); then
        echo "mrun: no command given. Try: mrun -- echo hi" >&2
        echo "      For an interactive shell session use: shere" >&2
        return 2
    fi

    [[ -z "$name" ]] && name=$(_mrun_default_name)
    name=$(_sesh_sanitize "$name")

    case "$backend" in
        tmux)
            command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 \
                || { echo "mrun: tmux not installed." >&2; return 1; }
            _mrun_tmux "$name" "$workdir" "$no_detach" "$@"
            ;;
        zellij)
            command -v zellij >/dev/null 2>&1 \
                || { echo "mrun: zellij not installed." >&2; return 1; }
            _mrun_zellij "$name" "$workdir" "$no_detach" "$@"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "mrun: unknown backend '$backend' (expected tmux or zellij)." >&2
            return 2
            ;;
    esac
}

function tmrun() { mrun -b tmux   "$@"; }
function zjrun() { mrun -b zellij "$@"; }
```

## Edge cases & pitfalls (additions to user's list)

1. **`mktemp -t` template difference.** Linux `mktemp` accepts `-t mrun-XXXXXX` and resolves under `$TMPDIR`. macOS `mktemp -t prefix` requires the prefix not to contain `XXXXXX`; the `XXXXXX` part is auto-added. Test on both — the form `mktemp -t mrun-layout` works on both, but to be safe use `mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/mrun-layout-XXXXXX"` (full template). Updated in sketch.

2. **Zellij `attach --create` vs `--new-session-with-layout`.** From `zellij --help`:
   - `zellij attach --create NAME` creates and attaches.
   - `zellij --layout FOO attach --create NAME` creates with the given layout if the session doesn't exist; attaches if it does.
   This is the cleaner spawn (validates the user's "no single CLI flag" finding — there isn't one, but `--layout` + `attach --create` is the documented path). The user's note about `zellij -s NAME -n LAYOUT` is also correct and works, but `--layout … attach --create` is what the zellij docs recommend.

3. **`zellij list-sessions` output format.** Modern zellij prefixes with ANSI color codes. Use `zellij list-sessions --no-formatting --short` or strip with `awk`. The dispatcher uses `awk '{print $1}'` which works for both.

4. **`$SHELL` vs `sh`.** I picked `sh` for portability and to mirror `system(3)` semantics. If the user has `set -o pipefail` muscle memory, they'll want bash. Counter-argument: `sh -c "bash -c '...'"` works as escape hatch. Sticking with `sh`.

5. **Default `default_mode "locked"` in zellij config.** New sessions inherit it. For a "run a CI command" use case this is fine. The user can override per-session by adding `default_mode "normal"` inside the generated layout — possible enhancement but not in v1.

6. **Session name uniqueness.** `_mrun_default_name` uses `$RANDOM % 65536`. Two `mrun` calls in the same second from the same dir collide with probability ~1/65536. Acceptable. Refusing on collision (sketch above) gives a clean error.

7. **`--` is optional but the help promotes it.** Without `--`, `mrun -n foo bar baz` parses correctly (bar is the command). With `mrun -- -n foo` you can run a command literally named `-n` if such a thing existed.

8. **Tmux nested: `$TMUX` set but user passes `-b zellij`.** Fine — zellij spawns in a parallel multiplexer, no warning needed (they're different tools).

9. **Already-failed command:** if the inner command exits immediately (typo), the tmux session disappears (default `remain-on-exit off`). The user sees `tmux attach -t foo` fail with "no such session" — hint should mention `tmux set -g remain-on-exit on` for debugging? **Counter:** the user's existing `_sesh_on_exit_wrap` pattern handles this for sesh-managed sessions. For mrun ("fire and forget") I'd argue the failure mode of "session vanishes silently" is a feature, not a bug — that's fire-and-forget. Don't add wrap here. Document in help text? Maybe one line: `Note: with default tmux config, sessions vanish on command exit. Add 'set -g remain-on-exit on' or use --no-detach to debug.`

10. **Quoting in `tmux new-session "...sh -c CMD..."`.** I used zsh's `${(q)var}` for the inner quote. Validate this on macOS zsh 5.9 — should be fine, it's been stable for a decade. The alternative is to construct via `tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$workdir" sh -c "$cmd"` (no outer string), which tmux supports — actually cleaner, let me revise:

```zsh
# Cleaner tmux invocation: pass argv directly (tmux exec's argv when given
# multiple args after -n).
tmux new-session -d -s "$session" -c "$workdir" -n run sh -c "$(printf '%s ' "$@")"
```

Even cleaner, no nested quoting. Pseudo-code revision noted.

## Unresolved questions worth asking the user

1. **Should `mrun` reject when CMD looks like an interactive editor (`nvim`, `vim`, `less`, `htop`)?** Detached interactive TUI = harmless if you intend to attach later, but a frequent footgun. My default: **don't reject** (fire-and-forget includes "open vim and come back"). But if the user has had this footgun before, a soft warn is cheap. — *Worth one yes/no question.*

2. **Should `mrun` default to overwrite (kill+recreate) on session-name collision, or fail loud?** Sketch above fails loud (return 1 with hint). Alternative: `mrun -f|--force` flag for kill-then-recreate. *Worth asking which the user prefers as default behavior.*

3. **Zellij detach mechanism: trust `setsid`/`nohup` fallback (current sketch), or run zellij with `--detach`-style backgrounding via `zellij attach --create-background`?** The user's research found `--create-background` creates an *empty* session — but combined with `zellij run` post-hoc into the new session, we could avoid the layout-file dance entirely. Trade-off: two-step (create empty + `zellij --session NAME run -- CMD`) vs one-step (layout file). The layout-file path is more atomic and supports cwd; the two-step is simpler but has a race window. *Worth asking which approach to use, OR I commit to layout-file as written and document the alternative in code comments.*

- Zellij CLI surface for "detached create at cwd, run command":
  - `zellij attach --create-background SESSION` — creates an EMPTY detached session, **no cwd/cmd args**.
  - `zellij run -- CMD` — opens a pane in the CURRENT session. Useless for "from outside, create new detached".
  - `zellij -s SESSION -n LAYOUT` (`--new-session-with-layout`) — starts a NEW session, but **foregrounds (attaches) you**.
  - There is NO single CLI flag that says "create-detached-with-command-and-cwd". The only way to express cwd + command is via a layout `.kdl` file (`pane cwd="…" { command "…" args "…" }`).
- Therefore the only way to get tmux-parity behavior on zellij is: generate an ephemeral layout KDL → spawn `zellij -s NAME -n LAYOUT` detached via `setsid -f` (Linux) / `nohup … & disown` (macOS — `setsid(1)` CLI is not in base macOS, see `pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md`).

**Repo conventions:**
- `_sesh_sanitize` already strips `.`, `:`, whitespace → `-`. Reuse it.
- `dot_config/zsh/tools/03_tmux_capture.zsh:27` is the existing precedent for guarding on `$TMUX`. No `$ZELLIJ` guard exists yet.
- `docs/zsh/aliases.md` table format (per CLAUDE.md contract): `| Command | Type | Source File | Description |`. Adding any new alias/function REQUIRES adding a row in the "Session Management" section.
- Source-order in `dot_config/zsh/tools/`: `22_sesh.zsh` defines sesh helpers; a new `23_mrun.zsh` file would be sourced after and could call `_sesh_sanitize`.

# Design questions I want you to answer

1. **One file or two?** Should this live in a new `dot_config/zsh/tools/23_mrun.zsh`, or appended to `22_sesh.zsh` next to the sesh helpers? Trade-off: separate file = clearer concern boundary; same file = easier reuse of private `_sesh_*` helpers + one spot for "session-create" logic. My lean is **new file 23_mrun.zsh** because mrun is its own concept (one-shot ephemeral runs, not project session layouts), and `_sesh_sanitize` can be called across files in the same shell. Validate or push back.

2. **Function shape — single dispatcher or two parallel functions?**
   - Option A: one function `mrun [-b tmux|zellij] [-n NAME] -- CMD ARG…`, env override `MRUN_BACKEND`, default tmux. Two thin aliases `tmrun` / `zjrun` that pin the backend.
   - Option B: two independent functions `tmrun` and `zjrun` that share one private helper `_mrun_session_name`.
   - Trade-off: A is DRY but requires arg parsing for `-b`. B is two short functions, easier to read, less tempting to over-generalize. Pick one and justify.

3. **Argument parsing.** Pick a final signature, including:
   - How NAME is supplied: `-n NAME` flag, or first positional, or always auto-derived (`run/$(basename PWD)`)?
   - How CMD is delimited: require `--` separator, or take everything after the flags?
   - What happens with no command at all? (My take: print usage + exit 2 — there's no value in creating a detached shell, that's `sesh-here`.)
   - Edge case: command contains shell metacharacters / quotes. tmux's `new-session ... CMD` runs the rest as one argv, so for safety the helper should pass through `$@` not a re-joined string.

4. **Nesting policy.** If `$TMUX` is set and backend=tmux, do we:
   - (a) refuse with a hint ("you're already in tmux; use `tmux new-window CMD`")?
   - (b) silently use `tmux new-session -d` anyway (which works, just creates an unrelated detached session)?
   - (c) detect and offer `tmux new-window` as a fallback inside the same session?
   Same question for `$ZELLIJ` + backend=zellij. My lean: **(b) — just create the detached session anyway**, because the whole point is "fire and forget"; nesting is fine and tmux handles it. But warn (single-line stderr note) so the user knows.

5. **Zellij backend implementation detail.** Validate the layout-file approach:
   - Generate KDL into `$(mktemp -t mrun-layout-XXXXXX.kdl)`.
   - KDL body:
     ```
     layout {
         tab name="run" {
             pane cwd="<absolute cwd>" {
                 command "<argv0>"
                 args "<arg1>" "<arg2>" …
             }
         }
     }
     ```
   - Spawn: `setsid -f zellij -s "$session" -n "$layout" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1` on Linux; `(nohup zellij -s "$session" -n "$layout" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &) ; disown 2>/dev/null` on macOS where `setsid(1)` isn't in base.
   - **Open question for you:** does the layout file need to stick around for the lifetime of the session, or does zellij read it once and then it can be deleted? If it's read once we should `rm` after a `sleep 0.5` in the background. Search for prior art / docs on this if uncertain — but if uncertain, keep the file around and let `/tmp` GC handle it.
   - **Open question:** quoting `args` — KDL strings need backslash-escaping of `"` and `\`. Is there a simpler way (heredoc + printf)?
   - Note: zellij `command` needs a real binary path, not a shell builtin or pipeline. If the user passes `mrun -- foo | bar`, that pipeline must run under a shell. Recommendation: **always wrap as `command "sh"` + `args "-c" "<full original cmd>"`** so the user can pass arbitrary shell syntax, mirroring tmux's behavior of running CMD via the user's default shell.
   - Cross-reference `pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md` to see if there's a documented portable detach helper we can reuse.

6. **Attach hint.** After spawning, print a single line like:
   - tmux: `Attach with: tmux attach -t <session>` (or `tmux switch-client -t` if already inside tmux).
   - zellij: `Attach with: zellij attach <session>`.
   This is non-negotiable — it's the whole point of the helper. Confirm exact wording.

7. **Aliases.** What short aliases to add (mirroring `shere`/`sroot`/`scode`/`svibe`)? My pick: `tmrun` (tmux-pinned), `zjrun` (zellij-pinned), and maybe `mrun` itself. The `m` in `mrun` collides with nothing per `command -v` checks I'd do at apply time.

8. **Docs updates.** Confirm the cross-file maintenance:
   - `docs/zsh/aliases.md`: one row per alias/function in Session Management section. Confirm format.
   - `CLAUDE.md` "Custom aliases & shell functions" section already covers this — no CLAUDE.md edit needed.
   - Should we add anything to `docs/tools/sesh.md` to cross-link? My lean: no — mrun isn't sesh; mention it from `docs/zsh/aliases.md` only.

9. **Verification plan.** Walk through how the user (or I) would manually verify each backend works end-to-end. Include the exact commands.

 `./pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md`

```text
1	# Shared sudo session re-prompts once per run-script on macOS (`setsid` missing)
2	
3	**Symptoms** (grep this section):
4	- On macOS, `chezmoi apply` (or `chezmoi update --init`) prompts three times
5	  in a row — once per run-script — despite the "entered once, reused for this
6	  chezmoi apply" wording:
7	  ```
8	  [bootstrap] sudo password for <user> (entered once, reused for this chezmoi apply):
9	  …
10	  [ansible]   sudo password for <user> (entered once, reused for this chezmoi apply):
11	  …
12	  [brew]      sudo password for <user> (entered once, reused for this chezmoi apply):
13	  ```
14	- `which setsid` on macOS: `setsid not found`
15	- `man 2 setsid` exists (libc system call), but `setsid(1)` does not ship in
16	  base macOS
17	- Between prompts, `$TMPDIR/chezmoi-sudo-$UID/` exists with valid `sudo.pass`
18	  / `ansible-become.yml` / `keepalive.pid`, but the PID in `keepalive.pid` is
19	  dead: `kill -0 $(cat …/keepalive.pid)` returns non-zero, `ps -p <pid>`
20	  returns no row
21	- Linux hosts (Ubuntu, Debian) are unaffected — util-linux ships `setsid(1)`
22	- No `setsid: command not found` error is visible to the user because the
23	  failing command is backgrounded with `>/dev/null 2>&1 &`
24	
25	**First seen**: 2026-04 on `Da-Weis-Mac-mini` (macOS 26.2 arm64, chezmoi 2.69.4)
26	**Affects**: any macOS host running `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` without
27	util-linux installed from Homebrew. Introduced when the shared-sudo helper
28	landed.
29	**Status**: fixed in `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` (`_sudo_spawn_watchdog`
30	falls back to `nohup` when `setsid` is unavailable).
31	
32	## Symptom
33	
34	The helper's contract is "prompt once at the start of `chezmoi apply`,
35	downstream run-scripts reuse the cached credential silently" (see
36	[CLAUDE.md → Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts](../CLAUDE.md)).
37	On macOS the prompt fires three separate times — once for `bootstrap`, once
38	for `ansible`, once for `brew` — with the state dir being wiped and rebuilt
39	between each.
40	
41	The state on disk during the second prompt looks "valid":
42	
43	```
44	$ ls -la "$TMPDIR/chezmoi-sudo-$(id -u)"
45	.rw-------@ 36 daviddwlee84 25 Apr 03:59  ansible-become.yml
46	.rw-------@  6 daviddwlee84 25 Apr 03:59  chezmoi.pid
47	.rw-------@  6 daviddwlee84 25 Apr 03:59  keepalive.pid
48	.rw-------@  9 daviddwlee84 25 Apr 03:59  sudo.pass
49	
50	$ PID=$(cat "$TMPDIR/chezmoi-sudo-$(id -u)/keepalive.pid")
51	$ kill -0 "$PID" 2>&1 || echo DEAD
52	DEAD
53	$ ps -p "$PID"
54	  PID TTY           TIME CMD       # empty — process long gone
55	```
56	
57	`sudo.pass` is correct; `ansible-become.yml` is correct; the watchdog is the
58	only broken piece.
59	
60	## Root cause
61	
62	`_sudo_spawn_watchdog` in `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` spawned the keepalive
63	watchdog via:
64	
65	```bash
66	setsid bash -c '…' _ "$state_dir" "$watch_pid" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
67	local pid=$!
68	```
69	
70	The goal was "new session, detached from the controlling TTY, survives the
71	invoking run-script's exit." On Linux `setsid(1)` does that. On macOS there
72	is no `setsid(1)` in base — Apple ships `setsid(2)` as a libc system call
73	(accessible from C, Python's `start_new_session=True`, etc.) but no CLI
74	wrapper. Homebrew has a keg-only `util-linux` formula which would provide
75	it, but this repo doesn't force-link it and most Macs don't have it.
76	
77	When `setsid` isn't on `$PATH`, the backgrounded invocation does this:
78	
79	1. Shell forks a child to run `setsid bash -c '…' &`
80	2. The child tries to `execvp("setsid", …)`, fails with `ENOENT`
81	3. Child prints `setsid: command not found` → redirected to `/dev/null` →
82	   invisible
83	4. Child exits with status 127 → zombie reaped by shell
84	5. Parent sets `pid=$!` to that dead child's PID (correct PID, dead process)
85	6. Parent writes that PID into `keepalive.pid`
86	
87	On the next run-script, `_sudo_state_valid` checks:
88	
89	```bash
90	kill -0 "$pid" 2>/dev/null || return 1   # ← fails here: PID is dead
91	```
92	
93	Returns non-zero → `sudo_session_init` thinks the state is stale → line 236
94	`rm -rf "$dir"` wipes the still-valid password files → re-prompt.
95	
96	The `sudo -S -v -p ''` validation a few lines later (line 110) would have
97	worked — `sudo.pass` is fine — but the `kill -0` check runs first and
98	short-circuits.
99	
100	## Workaround
101	
102	Fixed in-tree. The fix in `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` is to detect `setsid`
103	at runtime and fall back to `nohup` on systems without it:
104	
105	```bash
106	if command -v setsid >/dev/null 2>&1; then
107	    setsid bash -c "$body" _ "$state_dir" "$watch_pid" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
108	else
109	    nohup bash -c "$body" _ "$state_dir" "$watch_pid" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
110	fi
111	```
112	
113	Plus `trap "" HUP` at the top of the child body so SIGHUP on controlling-TTY
114	hangup is ignored even in the `nohup` branch (belt-and-suspenders — `nohup`
115	already does this, but making it explicit in the body means the behaviour
116	is identical between the two branches).
117	
118	`nohup` is in base macOS (`/usr/bin/nohup`) and in util-linux on Linux, so
119	this fallback is universally available. It doesn't create a new session
120	like `setsid` does, but for the actual requirement here ("survive the
121	parent run-script's exit") the `&` + `disown` + stdin/stdout/stderr-to-
122	`/dev/null` + SIGHUP-ignored combination is sufficient.
123	
124	Verification on a fresh `chezmoi apply` after the fix:
125	
126	```bash
127	$ grep -c 'sudo password' <apply-log>    # should be 1, not 3
128	1
129	
130	$ PID=$(cat "$TMPDIR/chezmoi-sudo-$(id -u)/keepalive.pid")
131	$ kill -0 "$PID" && echo alive
132	alive
133	```
134	
135	If you're debugging a machine that already has the stale state dir, wipe it
136	manually before the next apply:
137	
138	```bash
139	rm -rf "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/chezmoi-sudo-$(id -u)"    # or $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR on Linux
140	```
141	
142	## Prevention
143	
144	- Any new "detach a long-lived helper from this shell" in this repo must
145	  either use the pattern above (setsid-with-nohup-fallback) or go through
146	  a launchd agent. Don't add raw `setsid` calls to new shell scripts.
147	- When reviewing future edits to `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh`, check the
148	  watchdog spawn on macOS too — Linux CI passes silently for this class of
149	  bug because `setsid` always works there. The CLAUDE.md invariant "Sudo
150	  session is shared across all run-scripts" covers the `sudo -k` footgun
151	  but not the silent-watchdog-death footgun; this pitfall is the record.
152	- Long-term option: install util-linux via Homebrew in the ansible
153	  `devtools` role on macOS, symlink `setsid` into `~/.local/bin`. Not
154	  worth the keg-only linking complexity right now; the `nohup` fallback is
155	  simpler and less invasive.
156	
157	## Related
158	
159	- [CLAUDE.md → Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts](../CLAUDE.md) —
160	  the invariant this pitfall is a failure mode of
161	- [`docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md`](../docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md) —
162	  helper API, state dir layout, cleanup model
163	- [`scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh`](../scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh) —
164	  `_sudo_spawn_watchdog` is where the fix lives
165	- Apple's `setsid(2)` man page confirms the syscall exists but a CLI
166	  wrapper is not shipped — this is Apple's choice, not an oversight, so
167	  the workaround needs to live in this repo indefinitely
168
```
</details></tool-use>
